Remaining-game counts differ by team (byes already taken, Hawaii 13-game exemption, cancelled games), and conference title games do not count.
cfb.stat_leader_field_simulation.measurement: Field = all players within 3 standard deviations of the leader's projected total; for KXNCAAFLEADER ('Division I') the field includes FCS players until C-U2 settles FBS-only scope (FCS stats from stats.ncaa.org). For each, per-game production ~ negative binomial (yards: gamma on carries/targets x per-opportunity yards) with mean built here from cfb.player_usage share x script-adjusted team volume x per-opportunity efficiency adjusted by cfb.dvp for each remaining opponent (cfb.leader_race_state supplies only current totals and games remaining, so projection happens once) and dispersion fitted per position; shared team shock (log-normal SD fitted from team pace residuals) and teammate usage constraint (team carries or targets fixed per simulated game). Remaining games from the official schedule up to the last regular-season week; participation from the hazard input. 20,000 draws; output P(sole leader), P(tied N-way). As-of the prior Sunday.
free_sources: CFBD player game stats and schedules (free key)
raw_data: player game logs: carries, targets, receptions, yards, passing TD, sacks
team schedules with season_type and week

cfb.starting_job_loss_risk.label: Starting-job loss and QB-competition risk (non-injury)
cfb.starting_job_loss_risk.mechanism: Probability that a candidate loses his starting role or carry/target/rush-snap share to a teammate through benching, QB competition, transfer-portal arrivals or a coaching change, without any injury.
cfb.starting_job_loss_risk.rationale: Passing-TD leaders are quarterbacks and quarterback races are decided by benching as often as by injury, while feature backs lose carries to portal arrivals; an injury-only hazard under-disperses the leader field and over-states the incumbent, especially early in the season. Job loss is persistent (absorbing until a later injury) unlike a missed game.
cfb.starting_job_loss_risk.measurement: Per candidate and remaining week: P(job loss) = logistic of (depth-chart OR flag, prior-season snap share below 60 percent, presence of a portal or five-star replacement at the position, new head coach or coordinator flag, team losing streak of 3+ games, QB passer-rating rank within team), fit on FBS 2014+ starting-QB and RB1 changes with 8-week hazard windows; shrink to a position base rate with prior strength 40 team-seasons. Output a weekly hazard and the share of volume lost on job loss from the replacement's historical share; as-of prior Sunday.
free_sources: CFBD rosters, player usage and games (free key)
raw_data: starting QB and RB1 by game 2014+
player season snap or usage shares

game_side.mechanism: College moneyline, spread and half/quarter side markets price the distribution of margin: opponent-adjusted team strength (efficiency, talent, QB), venue and travel, schedule spots and motivation shift the mean, while tails are fatter than in the NFL because of mismatches, blowout management and variable pace. Roster churn from the portal, no reliable injury feed and cross-conference connectivity make priors and calibration central.
game_side.target: Probability a team wins, covers a spread rung, or leads at a period end, under the contract's regulation/overtime wording.

inputs.why: Market-implied strength anchors the prior and absorbs sharp information.
Composite ratings give an independent strength estimate and benchmark.
Opponent-adjusted offense efficiency drives scoring margin.
Opponent-adjusted defense efficiency completes the margin estimate.
Conference-level offsets prevent weak-schedule inflation in adjusted stats.
QB identity at decision time shifts margin by points.
Availability news (sparse) changes strength late.
Home-field effects vary widely; neutral sites remove them.
Short weeks, byes and travel create small effects.
Rivalry, bowl, playoff stakes and opt-outs.
Favorite behavior with large leads changes cover probabilities for big spreads.
Fat-tailed margin residuals and key numbers.
Overtime has no ties but extends the game; wording matters.
Sharp reference lines for benchmarking.
Regulation vs OT inclusion and period definitions.
Roster churn from the portal makes last season's results a weaker guide, especially early in the season.
Quote history shows how fast the market absorbs QB news.

interactions.hypothesis: QB status interacts with team strength and spread size: a QB change in college moves the line more than in the NFL because depth drops sharply behind the starter.
Spread size interacts with blowout management: for 21+ point favorites, cover probability depends on the coach's second-half behavior as much as on strength.
Conference calibration interacts with adjusted efficiency: cross-conference matchups are where raw adjusted stats are least reliable.

period.mechanism: Half and quarter markets inherit the game-level strength model with period-specific structure: scripted openers and opening-possession order, first-half vs second-half style (starters in/out, blowout management), halftime adjustments and end-of-half drives. Period scores are smaller and lumpier so ties and zero scoring have material mass; spreads on halves use margin distributions at period end.
period.target: Points, margin, winner or total in a period (first/second half, quarter) with tie handling per contract.

inputs.why: Opponent-adjusted period scoring rates.
First/second half scoring split by team and spread bucket.
Opening possession order and deferral behavior.
Opening-drive scripts and outcomes.
Early scripting and state-dependent pace.
Second-half starter removal reduces favorite scoring.
Plays per period scale scoring.
Implied team scoring allocated to periods.
Coach tempo and halftime management.
FG probability in short periods.
Tie and push rules per period.

interactions.hypothesis: Opening possession interacts with scripted first drives: the first-quarter edge is concentrated in teams with high first-drive scoring rates.
Spread size interacts with half split: big favorites score a larger share of points early, so first-half totals and spreads scale faster than game spread.
Tempo interacts with clock rules: fast teams get more possessions per period, and clock-rule regime changes alter the effect.

game_total.mechanism: Totals combine possessions (tempo of both offenses, turnover and punt rates, clock rules) with points per possession from opponent-adjusted PPA, explosiveness, red-zone finishing, field position and kicking, modified by weather, venue and lineup (QB). College totals have huge variance in pace and style, fat tails from mismatches, and favorite blowout management; team totals are slices of the same joint distribution.
game_total.target: Total or team points exceeding a threshold in regulation (or including overtime per wording).

inputs.why: Tempo of both offenses sets plays; ranges wide in college.
Expected possessions and plays per drive are the base unit of scoring; explosive teams have few plays but many scoring drives.
Own offense PPA, adjusted for opponents and recency, gives points per drive for each side.
Opponent defense PPA suppresses points per drive and must be adjusted for conference connectivity.
Success rate versus explosiveness determines drive length and the variance of the total.
Red-zone TD versus FG conversion changes points per scoring trip and regresses strongly in college sample sizes.
Starting field position and special teams change expected points per drive and short-field scoring chances.
Kicker range and accuracy decide how many stalled drives yield 3 points and create key-number structure in totals.
QB identity at decision time shifts both offense efficiency and pace, and is often confirmed late.
Wind and rain forecast vintages reduce passing and FG success, with open-air stadiums most exposed.
The clock-rule regime in the season determines plays per game and thus the baseline of scoring for the sample.
Starter removal and clock running by a leading favorite cut late scoring, while the underdog collects garbage-time points.
Total residuals by spread and total bucket give fat-tailed probabilities for each rung and key-number mass.
Sharp sportsbook totals embed weather and lineup information; the Kalshi total ladder should be compared with them after de-vig.
Adjacent total rungs imply a distribution; kinks or non-monotone quotes identify stale rungs and avoid double-counting correlated bets.

interactions.hypothesis: Tempo of both teams interacts with clock rules: the effect of a no-huddle offense is partially offset by an opponent that controls the clock with the run.
Wind and rain interact with passing style: air-raid offenses lose more efficiency than run-heavy teams, so weather impact on totals is style-dependent.
Mismatch size interacts with total: the favorite's late pace and the underdog's garbage-time scoring determine the net effect on totals.

game_event.mechanism: Game-event and stat props (overtime, team/game statistics) depend on the same drive and score process, with additional style and rules factors: regulation tie probability and overtime rules for overtime markets, pace and pass/run mix for yardage and count stats, and havoc/pressure for sacks and turnovers. College stat counts have scoring-source ambiguity (e.g. sack yardage in rushing) that matters for settlement.
game_event.target: Occurrence or count of a game-level event or team statistic as defined by contract.

inputs.why: Mass at zero margin for overtime events.
Overtime rules and tie probability determine overtime markets and any event defined over extra periods.
Counting events (TDs, sacks, penalties, yards) scale with plays, and college tempo varies widely between teams.
Pass/run mix determines yardage categories.
Sack and pressure rates for and against determine sack and negative-play counts.
Havoc rates predict TFLs, forced fumbles and pass breakups, which feed turnover and negative-play counts.
Takeaway counts are heavily luck-driven, so realized turnover margin must be regressed before pricing turnover events.
Red-zone finishing determines TD versus FG counts and TD-count events.
Expected team scoring sets the base for TD counts and scoring-based events.
Weather shifts passing, fumbles and kicking events with known forecast timing.
Penalty-related events depend on crew and conference flag rates and team discipline.
Statistic definitions and source.
Event labels come from settled outcomes, not approximations.

interactions.hypothesis: Tie mass interacts with total and spread: overtime is most likely in close, low-scoring, kicker-driven games.
Pass rush interacts with protection and QB mobility: sack counts concentrate in matchups with dominant rush versus weak OL and immobile QB.
Havoc interacts with turnover luck: takeaways counts regress unless supported by process (PBU, pressure).

player_other.mechanism: College player props (TD scorer, yardage, receptions) = volume x efficiency: volume from team plays and script (spread), target/carry share and depth chart roles; efficiency from opponent-adjusted skill and the matchup. Rotation depth, blowouts, QB mobility, scheme style and sparse availability data mean wider variance and greater role uncertainty than the NFL.
player_other.target: Probability a player scores or exceeds a statistical threshold under the contract definition.

inputs.why: Share of targets/carries/snaps by role.
Role-based scoring rates combine red-zone and goal-line usage with team expected TDs.
Total plays scale the volume available to individual players.
Pass versus run split determines whether volume flows to receivers or backs.
Spread-implied script shifts volume between passing and rushing and between starters and backups.
Starters leave lopsided games early, capping counting stats for favorites' players.
Teammate availability redistributes targets and carries, and depth is thin in college.
Opponent-adjusted position defense.
QB rushing competes for carries and TDs.
Distribution shape (rotation, blowouts, boom-bust usage) determines exceedance probability at each rung.
Depth chart clarity and recent changes identify role stability and starter status.
Contract treatment of non-participation (void versus loss) and how stats are counted (e.g. sacks) define settlement.
Official and provider stats differ in definitions and corrections, producing label noise near thresholds.
Realized hit rates by rung calibrate player-prop ladders.

interactions.hypothesis: Spread and blowout management: a large favorite's RB1 gets early volume but loses late carries to backups, reducing counting-stat ceilings.
QB mobility and goal-line usage: dual-threat QBs absorb red-zone carries, lowering RB and WR TD probability.
Opponent matchup and role: slot receivers vs weak nickel corners gain share more than outside receivers vs average defenses.

season_outcome.mechanism: Season-level college outcomes (conference title, playoff berth, rankings, awards, national title) derive from team strength with uncertainty, the unbalanced schedule, tiebreakers and a selection process (committee/format) that adds non-statistical judgement; format changes and conference realignment change structure; roster churn and QB injuries dominate preseason uncertainty.
season_outcome.target: Season-level event resolution (title, berth, ranking, award) under contract definition.

inputs.why: Simulation of conference race and tiebreakers.
Format and seeding rules in force.
Time-varying market-implied strength with uncertainty is the base for simulations and futures prices.
Composite ratings provide an independent strength estimate and a check against the market-implied rating.
Preseason regression and returning production.
Forward-looking opponent strength over an unbalanced schedule drives expected wins and tiebreaker paths.
Lucky one-score records inflate rankings and perceived strength and regress going forward.
Ranking dynamics and committee behavior.
QB injury or change is the dominant single risk for a contender's season distribution.
Constraints across linked markets.
Sportsbook futures give benchmark probabilities after de-vig, though vig-heavy and sparse for small outcomes.
Contract defines eligibility, cancelled-game handling and which ranking or source resolves the market.

interactions.hypothesis: Committee behavior interacts with record and strength: playoff berth probability depends on both results and committee preferences (quality wins, strength of record).
Roster continuity interacts with schedule: teams with low returning production and tough early schedules have wider win distributions.
Luck regression interacts with rankings: lucky records inflate polls and rankings, so regress before projecting.

game_moneyline_spread.label: Game moneyline and spread
game_moneyline_spread.target: Probability a team wins (regulation plus overtime; no ties) or covers a spread rung.
game_moneyline_spread.mechanism: Margin mean = opponent-adjusted rating difference (efficiency, talent, QB-specific) + home or neutral-site edge + rest/travel/motivation, with fat tails and key numbers. Because college connectivity is thin and injury information is sparse, the market-implied rating is the primary prior and the model searches for incremental information: QB status, availability, weather, scheme style, and blowout behavior at large spreads. Overtime is certain to produce a winner so moneyline has no tie leg.

inputs.why: Market-implied rating as prior.
Composite ratings give a second strength estimate that checks the market-implied rating and highlights disagreements.
Opponent-adjusted offensive PPA is the structural scoring component of the margin independent of market lines.
Opponent-adjusted defensive PPA completes the margin estimate and matters more for matchups against specific offenses.
Cross-conference connectivity correction.
Talent ceiling and depth, important at extremes and early season.
Early-season regression of last year's ratings.
The QB identity vintage determines whether the model assumes the starter; changes can move the line by several points.
Sparse availability information (conference reports and beat reporters) can change strength late; vintage tracking avoids look-ahead.
Line continuity and injuries change pass protection and run blocking and are under-reported in college.
Teams with lucky turnover margins are overrated by results-based ratings and regress.
Home-field strength varies widely and neutral sites (bowls, rivalry neutral) remove it.
Byes, short weeks, long travel and kickoff time shift the margin slightly.
Rivalry, bowl, playoff stakes and opt-outs change effort and lineup in specific games.
Large-favorite coaches pull starters and run clock, capping margins in ways that matter for big-spread covers.
Weather increases margin variance and reduces passing teams' advantage.
Margin distribution and key numbers.
Sharp sportsbook sides are the benchmark; deviations in Kalshi quotes show staleness or lag after news.
Spread rungs imply a margin distribution; inconsistent rungs signal stale quotes and shared risk across adjacent covers.
Portal arrivals and departures change starters and unit quality, and eligibility rulings can be decided late.
Bowl and playoff opt-outs and four-game-redshirt decisions remove starters from specific late games.
Suspensions and first-half targeting carryovers remove players for a game or half and are only partly in feeds.
Quote history shows when the market absorbs QB, weather and lineup news and benchmarks closing-line value.
Depth and spread determine whether a modeled edge is executable.
Fees reduce edge, especially near 50c where fee per contract peaks.
Volume and open interest signal price reliability and feasible size.
Executed trades reveal real fills and informed flow versus stale quotes.
Open/close/halt and postponement events (including weather delays) define the information set.
A dominant pass rush against a weak line ends drives and shortens the favourite's margin; the matchup term is the rush rate for versus the line's sack rate allowed.
Explosive pass offences against thin secondaries produce large margins that efficiency averages understate.
Run-heavy favourites against weak fronts convert leads into clock; margin distributions skew toward key numbers.
Option and tempo offences compress possessions and transfer variance to the underdog, changing cover probability at constant rating gap.
Quarterback change is the biggest discrete news item in a college spread, and the replacement pool is thin and unevenly observed, so a point value with uncertainty is required, not just a flag.
Turns an unstructured injury list into the same unit as the spread, so a +/- 1.5 point late shift can be compared with the quote move rather than judged qualitatively.
Margin SD and the shape of P(cover) across rungs depend on rating uncertainty, which no existing input supplies.
The sampled KXNCAAFSPREAD and KXNCAAFWINMARGIN rungs reach 41.5 and 7-14 buckets; probabilities across 40 rungs must come from a calibrated truncated distribution, not a normal.
Coaching_scheme was uncovered for sides; aggression and clock management bend the margin distribution without changing its mean.

KXNCAAFSECWINS, BIGTENWINS, BIG12WINS and ACCWINS (sampled rungs 8+, 7+, 5+ teams with 10+ wins, regular season only per the rules text) need a joint schedule simulation, not a single-game margin model.
The sampled KXNCAAFHIGHSCORE rule is a Division I maximum including overtime, regular season only; one favourite game cannot price it.
KXNCAAFD3GAME and KXNCAAFCSGAME are winner markets on teams outside FBS data coverage; their probability comes from this score-based rating, not from SP+ or PPA.

interactions.hypothesis: QB status x spread: a QB change in college moves the line more because of depth and system fit; Kalshi quotes may lag the news, so timing of QB vintage matters.
Spread size x blowout management: cover probability for big favorites depends on whether the coach keeps pressing, shifting the tail of the margin distribution.
Tempo mismatch x efficiency: when a fast offense meets a slow, ball-control team, variance falls and margin shrinks; spreads with high rating gaps may overstate.
Early season: low returning production x talent prior: ratings carry large uncertainty; weight talent and portal data more than last year's results.

A backup quarterback behind a depleted offensive line loses more than the sum of the two separate effects because inexperienced passers rely on protection and play-action tied to a functioning run game; the penalty is largest when the replacement is a first-year player with fewer than 50 dropbacks.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit margin residual on replacement value, OL games-missed index and their product; compare slope on the product term in games with both vs one shock.

interactions.hypothesis: Past a lead of about 21 points in the second half the favourite's marginal scoring rate drops sharply for conservative coaches, while aggressive coaches keep scoring; this makes the cover rate for 30+ point rungs a coach-dependent step, not a smooth function of rating gap.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare realised P(margin >= 30) for games with gap > 28 split by aggression tercile; test a step at pre-game gap 21-24.

interactions.hypothesis: In weeks 1-4 the prior dominates, so talent and returning production explain more of the margin than in-season efficiency and the posterior SD is wide; from about week 8 the weights flip and the same variables become nearly redundant.
interactions.how_to_test: Rolling regression of margin on prior vs in-season rating by week; identify the crossing week and test stability across seasons.

interactions.hypothesis: Wind or rain compresses passing, which helps a run-heavy option team against a weak front and hurts an air-raid favourite; the weather effect on margin depends on which side is pass-reliant and on opposing run defence.
interactions.how_to_test: Interact style (pass share), wind speed above 15 mph and opponent run-defence rank in a margin residual model; check sign by pass-reliant favourite vs underdog.

interactions.hypothesis: Home-field value is not constant: it grows with altitude and crowd for visitors on a short week and shrinks in rivalry games where both teams are fully motivated; opt-outs at neutral-site bowls remove it altogether.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate home-edge by team and test interactions with days of rest and rivalry flag; neutral-site bowls as a control group.

interactions.hypothesis: In the D3 and FCS playoffs the higher seed hosts until the final, so the home edge is confounded with seed strength and applies only in rounds before the neutral-site final; a regular-season home edge applied to a playoff host overstates the favourite when both seed and host status carry the same information.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit the playoff home edge separately with seed difference as a covariate on D3 and FCS postseason games and compare with the regular-season estimate.

nonlinearities.shape: Concave in rating gap beyond ~21 points, with a floor from garbage-time scores
nonlinearities.why: Expected margin does not grow one-for-one with rating gap once starters sit, so P(margin >= 42) rises far more slowly than a Gaussian predicts and differs by opponent class.

nonlinearities.shape: Inverse-square-root decay in games played, with a jump after portal-heavy offseasons
nonlinearities.why: Rating uncertainty shrinks with sample size but resets with roster churn; it changes win probability by several points at constant rating gap.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex in dropbacks of the replacement: very wide posterior below ~50 career dropbacks
nonlinearities.why: Swap cost for an unknown backup is a fat-tailed mixture, not a normal shift; the mean is little changed but the downside tail is heavy.

mechanism_review.summary: Final margin = true strength difference (opponent-adjusted offense and defense, each uncertain) + site effect + situational and availability shifts, plus a game-level noise term whose size grows with fewer possessions, high variance styles and weather. College football has thin connectivity, a very wide spread of team strength (spreads above 30 are common), and no reliable injury feed, so the prior and its uncertainty matter as much as the mean. The realized margin is then truncated and reshaped by script: favourites with big leads pull starters and run clock, trailing teams chase, and scoring comes in lumps of 3, 6, 7 and 8, so probabilities at adjacent half-point rungs differ by key-number mass. Moneyline settles on the winner after overtime (no ties), spread rungs on margin including overtime.

stages.name: Team-strength prior and its uncertainty
stages.description: Each team's true strength is a latent opponent-adjusted offensive and defensive efficiency, estimated from last season (shrunk by returning production, portal net gains and recruiting talent) and updated through the year. Connectivity across the 130-plus FBS teams is thin, so a Group-of-Five team's rating relative to a Power team is calibrated by few cross-conference games. The width of the estimate, not just its centre, matters for P(cover).
stages.distribution: Latent Gaussian rating with prior SD roughly 5-6 points in week 0 shrinking toward 2-3 by midseason; mean-reverting, heavy-tailed for teams with massive roster churn.

stages.name: Availability and personnel substitution
stages.description: Starting quarterback, offensive line and a handful of high-snap defenders determine the actual units on the field. Information is released late and partially (there is no mandatory injury report in most conferences), so what matters is both the expected points value of each loss and the vintage at which it became knowable. A quarterback swap is a discrete shift with a wide posterior on the replacement.
stages.distribution: Discrete shocks (zero most weeks, 3-10 point magnitude for a QB) with a mixture of confirmed and doubtful states; replacement quality is itself uncertain.

stages.name: Site, travel, weather and motivation adjustments
stages.description: A home-field term that differs by team (crowd, altitude, visiting travel and body clock), neutral-site games where it vanishes, short-week or bye effects, and games with unusual stakes such as rivalry, bowl eligibility or opt-outs. Weather mostly changes the variance and the run-pass balance of the game rather than the mean margin.
stages.distribution: Mostly small additive shifts (0.5-3 points) with a few large conditional ones (altitude visitors, bowl opt-outs); weather widens variance.

stages.name: Matchup-specific scoring process and variance
stages.description: Two teams of equal rating can produce different margin distributions: a pressure defence against a thin line, an explosive passing attack against a poor secondary, a run-heavy slow offence that shortens the game. Possession count and play style set how many independent scoring trials there are, which controls margin variance and thus underdog cover frequency, and head-coach aggression bends the tail of late scoring.
stages.distribution: Margin variance scales roughly with the number of possessions; style pairings create heteroscedastic, skewed margin errors rather than mean shifts.

stages.name: Game-script truncation and score lattice
stages.description: Once a lead exceeds roughly three scores, college coaches substitute starters, run the ball and burn clock, and trailing teams score late garbage points, so realized margins compress at high spreads relative to a Gaussian. Football scoring is lumpy (3, 6, 7, 8), producing mass on margins of 3, 7, 10 and 14 and differences between rungs such as 6.5 and 7.5. The final result includes overtime, which cannot end tied.
stages.distribution: Truncated, key-number-lumpy margin distribution with a right tail that depends on opponent class (FBS vs FCS) and on coach behaviour.

stages.name: Contract mechanics: strike, overtime scope and postponement
stages.description: Spread rungs are strict greater-than on a .5 strike, so the target is P(margin >= ceiling of the strike) with no push; WINMARGIN buckets are read as full game including overtime, while SPREAD and GAME overtime scope is not stated (CSGAME and D3GAME only say a declared tie pays 50/50). GAME, SPREAD and WINMARGIN stay open for a postponement that starts within 48 hours and otherwise resolve to a fair price; CSGAME and D3GAME stay open until a rescheduled game finishes within two weeks, then fair price, so the lifecycle feed defines the information set and the void-like state.
stages.distribution: Binary payoff per rung (bucket for WINMARGIN) as a deterministic function of the final margin; a small fair-price mass for long postponements.

stages.name: Division III and FCS winner markets from score-only ratings
stages.description: KXNCAAFD3GAME (for example North Central (IL) vs John Carroll) and KXNCAAFCSGAME (Montana at Montana St.) are winner markets on games outside FBS data coverage. The outcome is still margin > 0, but the margin mean must come from a score-based rating with weak inter-region connectivity, the home edge applies to the playoff host seed, and the margin spread is wider than in FBS because talent gaps are larger; dominant D3 programs produce very lopsided favourites. These historical texts also differ in edge-case wording: a tie pays 50/50 and a postponement stays open for up to two weeks.
stages.distribution: Probit in rating gap over a division-specific margin SD, with extra variance from rating uncertainty; probabilities near 0 or 1 for dominant programs.

talent_strength.note: Opponent-adjusted efficiency, talent and returning production feed the latent rating; rating_posterior_sd adds the uncertainty term the existing set lacked.

opponent_matchup.note: Unit-on-unit matchups; value is in crosses (rush rate vs protection) not levels.

role_personnel.note: Replacement quality at quarterback and snap-weighted loss across positions.

availability_news.note: Coverage rests on timestamped quarterback status, snap-weighted availability loss and eligibility news; cfb.injuries is WEAK (no official feed in most conferences) and removed, the feed gap is listed as injury_feed_gap.

coaching_scheme.note: Aggression and clock management plus scheme identity; coach-change resets are an open definition issue.

environment.note: Home field, altitude, neutral site and weather; kickoff body-clock effects are not separately defined.

game_context_script.note: Starter-removal and clock behaviour truncate large margins.

pace_volume.note: Possession count and tempo are measured by cfb.pace (seconds per play, plays per game, no-huddle rate) and cfb.drives (drives per game, plays per drive), crossed with offense_style and clock behaviour; the combined possession count sets margin variance.

efficiency_conversion.note: Per-play efficiency with a luck adjustment for fumble recoveries.

distribution_variance.note: Margin SD, truncation and key-number mass.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest, rivalry, bowl eligibility and opt-outs.

officiating_rules.note: Crew penalty tendencies move a game by about one or two penalties and under a point of margin; the one rule-driven item that matters (targeting ejection) is carried by cfb.suspension_eligibility, so no separate officiating input is justified for sides.

settlement_contract.note: Strict greater-than rungs, overtime inclusion and 48-hour postponement rule read from the sampled rules; ML and FCS series text is missing.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Five single-game side series, all with rules text. KXNCAAFGAME and KXNCAAFCSGAME/KXNCAAFD3GAME settle YES if the named team wins the game ('If Utah St. wins the Utah St. vs Oregon St. college football game'); the GAME text does not say whether overtime counts or what a tie pays, while the historical CSGAME and D3GAME texts say a declared tie resolves 50/50 and refer to the winner 'or participant awarded a tie'. KXNCAAFSPREAD settles YES if the named team wins by more than the half-point strike (Florida Atlantic by more than 41.5); overtime inclusion is not stated. KXNCAAFWINMARGIN settles on a bucket of final point differential in the 'Full game (including overtime)'. Postponement: GAME, SPREAD and WINMARGIN stay open if the game starts within 48 hours and otherwise resolve to a fair price; CSGAME and D3GAME stay open until a rescheduled game finishes within two weeks and otherwise resolve to a fair price. No statistics provider is named.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Kalshi text cites the official final result of the game; the specific Source Agency or stats provider is not named in the sampled rules for the game markets. NCAA and conference box scores are the likely truth, but the exact provider is unresolved.
variants_and_edge_cases: Two postponement regimes inside the archetype: GAME, SPREAD and WINMARGIN use a 48-hour start window then fair price; CSGAME and D3GAME (historical texts) keep the market open for a rescheduled game finished within two weeks, then fair price.
Tie handling is stated only in CSGAME and D3GAME (declared tie pays 50/50); KXNCAAFGAME and KXNCAAFSPREAD are silent, which matters little in FBS (overtime prevents ties) but is unread.
KXNCAAFWINMARGIN buckets are custom strikes ('Between 7 to 14 points'); inclusive endpoints at 7 and 14 are implied by the wording, but adjacent bucket boundaries are not shown in the sample.
KXNCAAFSPREAD says only 'wins by more than 41.5 points' and resolves on the official final result; overtime inclusion is not stated (contrast WINMARGIN 'Full game (including overtime)').
KXNCAAFD3GAME is a Division III playoff game (North Central (IL) vs John Carroll); team-strength data for D3 and FCS comes from scores only, not from FBS play-by-play.

game_total.label: Game total points
game_total.target: Probability that total points exceed a rung (regulation plus overtime per wording).
game_total.mechanism: Total = possessions x points per possession for both teams. In college, tempo spans a wider range, clock rules and style (option, air raid) change plays per game, and mismatch/blowout management lowers the favorite's late scoring while inflating variance; weather and QB identity are the main late-information drivers. Distribution has key numbers and fat right tail; the Kalshi ladder should be consistent with the implied distribution.

inputs.why: Both teams' tempo and no-huddle rates.
Expected possessions and plays per drive are the base unit of scoring; explosive teams have few plays but many scoring drives.
Pass share determines clock usage.
The clock-rule regime in the season determines plays per game and thus the baseline of scoring for the sample.
Own offense PPA, adjusted for opponents and recency, gives points per drive for each side.
Opponent defense PPA suppresses points per drive and must be adjusted for conference connectivity.
Success rate versus explosiveness determines drive length and the variance of the total.
Red-zone TD versus FG conversion changes points per scoring trip and regresses strongly in college sample sizes.
High havoc defenses create negative plays and turnovers that kill drives and cut totals.
Starting field position and special teams change expected points per drive and short-field scoring chances.
Kicker range and accuracy decide how many stalled drives yield 3 points and create key-number structure in totals.
QB identity at decision time shifts both offense efficiency and pace, and is often confirmed late.
Wind and rain forecast vintages reduce passing and FG success, with open-air stadiums most exposed.
Option or air-raid styles produce atypical plays per game and run/pass splits, shifting the total relative to efficiency ratings.
Starter removal and clock running by a leading favorite cut late scoring, while the underdog collects garbage-time points.
Penalty-heavy crews or conferences lengthen drives and change pace, with small effects.
Total residuals by spread and total bucket give fat-tailed probabilities for each rung and key-number mass.
Sharp sportsbook totals embed weather and lineup information; the Kalshi total ladder should be compared with them after de-vig.
Adjacent total rungs imply a distribution; kinks or non-monotone quotes identify stale rungs and avoid double-counting correlated bets.
Bowl lineups with opt-outs lower expected scoring relative to regular-season efficiency ratings.
Quote history shows when the market absorbs QB, weather and lineup news and benchmarks closing-line value.
Depth and spread determine whether a modeled edge is executable.
Fees reduce edge, especially near 50c where fee per contract peaks.
Volume and open interest signal price reliability and feasible size.
Executed trades reveal real fills and informed flow versus stale quotes.
Open/close/halt and postponement events (including weather delays) define the information set.
Labels should use settled totals with the contract's overtime handling, not recomputed scores.
Short fields from turnovers inflate points scored; a team's recent turnover margin beyond its fumble-recovery expectation regresses, so totals built on raw scoring carry a luck premium.
Replaces the average-of-paces approach with the structural number of scoring trials, the strongest single driver of a game total.
Splits efficiency into moving and finishing, important because totals depend on 3-versus-7 outcomes rather than yardage.
Fat-tail component of the total not captured by drive-based efficiency.
Makes the weather vintage input usable for totals by linking forecast to actual game conditions in the specific building.
KXNCAAFHIGHSCORE settles on whether any Division I regular-season game (overtime included) exceeds the strike, an extreme-value quantity over all game totals that a one-game total model cannot price.

interactions.hypothesis: Combined tempo: two fast teams compound plays and drives, but a slow opponent controls clock; model pace as an interaction rather than average.
Weather x style: wind/rain reduce points more for pass-heavy and explosive teams and affect FG range, so the total effect depends on both offenses' styles.
Blowout management x spread: large spreads lower the favorite's second-half scoring but raise underdog garbage-time points; net effect depends on coach behavior.
Success vs explosiveness x havoc: an explosive offense facing a high-havoc defense has more failed drives but more big plays, widening the total distribution.

Possession count depends on run share through the clock rules: a run-heavy team that keeps the clock moving after first downs shortens the game for both sides, and a pass-heavy opponent cannot restore the possessions because incompletions stop the clock only for its own snaps; so tempo of the faster team matters less when the slower team has a high run share.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress realised total possessions on each team seconds per play interacted with the combined run share and season clock regime; check whether the tempo coefficient shrinks as combined run share rises.

interactions.hypothesis: Wind above roughly 15 mph at an open stadium reduces both deep passing and field-goal range beyond 40 yards; the cut in total is minimal below the threshold and then steep, and is amplified when the kicker is already marginal.
interactions.how_to_test: Bucket games by adjusted on-field wind and kicker long-range accuracy; compare average total versus ratings-implied total.

interactions.hypothesis: In a one-sided game the total follows a different regime: the leader's scoring drops but the trailing team's garbage-time possessions and return touchdowns add points; whether the total goes up or down depends on the coach's pull point and on trailing-team passing.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the total residual for games with pre-game rating gap above 21 split by coach pull-point tercile and by trailing offence pass rate.

interactions.hypothesis: A high-explosiveness offence facing a high-havoc defence produces many failed drives but occasional long scores; the mean total changes little while its variance and right tail increase, which matters for high rungs.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare the variance of totals by explosiveness x havoc bucket; test with quantile regression at the 80th and 90th percentiles.

interactions.hypothesis: A quarterback change lowers both efficiency and tempo (backups run a simpler script), so the effect on the total is the product of a smaller points-per-drive and fewer possessions, and it is bigger for up-tempo offences.
interactions.how_to_test: Contrast pre/post-change totals for teams by tempo tercile, controlling for opponent and weather.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold near 15 mph on-field wind, steep beyond 20 mph
nonlinearities.why: Passing and kicking degrade slowly until wind affects the ball's flight, then drop steeply; a linear wind term misprices both calm and gale games.

nonlinearities.shape: Linear in count but with SD that grows with tempo; total points concave in possessions at high counts
nonlinearities.why: Extra possessions are not equal: late extra possessions occur in blowouts or garbage time with lower scoring rates, so marginal points per added possession declines.

nonlinearities.shape: Lumpy 0/3/7 per trip with convex value of touchdown conversion near the goal line
nonlinearities.why: Moving a trip from field goal to touchdown adds 4 points, and the probability gain is concentrated near the 10-yard line; small efficiency shifts have large point effects when concentrated there.

mechanism_review.summary: Total points = number of possessions x expected points per possession summed over both offences, plus non-offensive scores, with overtime as an optional extra if the contract counts it. Possessions come from tempo (seconds per play), run-pass mix and clock management, and are shared between the two teams so the slower side dominates; points per possession come from opponent-adjusted efficiency, finishing (touchdown versus field goal), field position and special teams. Late information (quarterback, weather) and game script (blowouts compress the favourite, garbage time adds underdog points) shape the distribution, which is right-skewed with key-number lumps. The HIGHSCORE series is a different functional of the same per-game process: the maximum of several hundred regular-season game totals, governed by the extreme right tail (mismatch shootouts, multi-overtime games) rather than by the centre of any one game.

stages.name: Possession count from joint tempo
stages.description: A game contains roughly 22 to 26 combined possessions in modern FBS. The count is set by both offences' seconds per play, plays per drive, run share and the clock regime (running clock after first downs since 2023), and by the lead size late; a slow ball-control team pulls a fast team's possessions down, so tempo combines harmonically rather than additively.
stages.distribution: Near-Gaussian count with SD of about 2 possessions; right tail in shootouts with turnovers and quick scores.

stages.name: Points per possession for each offence
stages.description: For each side, expected points per drive combine ability to move the ball (opponent-adjusted success and explosive plays), the quality of the opposing defence, starting field position and the finishing rate inside the 40. Finishing includes the touchdown versus field-goal choice and kicker range, and so the same yardage yields different points.
stages.distribution: Per-drive points are a 0/3/7 mixture; the sum over ~12 drives gives a total with SD of roughly 13 points, right-skewed by explosive drives.

stages.name: Late information on personnel and conditions
stages.description: Quarterback identity, kicker status and weather are confirmed late and move the total more than any rating. Wind and rain reduce passing and field-goal range but only at open stadiums; temperature and dome status matter at the margins. Officials contribute a small amount through penalty rate.
stages.distribution: Discrete shocks (QB change) plus continuous weather effects; weather impact is threshold-like in wind speed.

stages.name: Script compression and non-offensive scores
stages.description: When a favourite builds a large lead, starters leave and the clock runs, trimming its late scoring, while the underdog gets garbage-time possessions; the net depends on the coach. Defensive and special-teams touchdowns add points without an offensive drive and add dispersion; they are mostly luck with a small skill component.
stages.distribution: Mixture: the central mass is truncated by script compression, while rare 6-8 point lumps (return touchdowns) fatten the right tail.

stages.name: Overtime and contract definition
stages.description: If regulation ends tied (about 5 to 8 percent of games) overtime adds points: a two-possession period starting at the 25-yard line with about 4 to 5 expected points per side; whether those count is not stated in the sampled rules, which changes the probability of crossing a rung near the median by a few percentage points. Conditional input set: if overtime counts in KXNCAAFTOTAL, the total needs cfb.ot_model (P(tie after 60 minutes) from the margin and total distribution, overtime possession scoring, number of overtimes; the same inputs are defined in the overtime archetype as cfb.regulation_tie_curve and cfb.ot_possession_scoring_rate); if it does not, the series is regulation-only and cfb.ot_model drops out.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli tie event with discrete additive points in 3/6/7/8 lattice.

stages.name: Season maximum over all Division I game totals (HIGHSCORE)
stages.description: HIGHSCORE resolves on the largest single-game total of the regular season, so the quantity is an upper order statistic: the per-game exceedance probability above 144.5 is tiny and is driven by fast-tempo, weak-defence pairings and by overtime, then compounded across all remaining Division I games. Exposure (games left, maximum already observed) matters as much as the tail shape, and the modern two-point overtime format caps how much a long overtime adds.
stages.distribution: Generalised Pareto tail above roughly 95 points per game; season union probability 1 - prod(1 - p_g) over remaining games, with a multi-overtime mixture component.

talent_strength.note: Opponent-adjusted efficiency of both offences and defences; talent composite is in the catalog but not attached.

opponent_matchup.note: Style pairing and defensive havoc against the opposing line and protection.

availability_news.note: Late quarterback confirmation and bowl opt-outs; other injuries rely on catalog inputs not attached here.

coaching_scheme.note: Scheme and lead-management tendencies; fourth-down aggression is untested for totals.

efficiency_conversion.note: Moving the ball versus finishing; field-goal conversion.

distribution_variance.note: Right-skewed total with lumps at 3/7 and a return-touchdown tail. HIGHSCORE uses the season-maximum tail (cfb.season_max_total_tail).

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest, lookahead, rivalry and conference-championship stakes shift effort and tempo but nothing in this archetype's inputs captures them for totals; their effect size on totals is unmeasured.

officiating_rules.note: Crew penalty tendency and the season clock regime.

settlement_contract.note: Strict greater-than, overtime inclusion unresolved, 48-hour postponement clause.

contract_review.settlement_definition: KXNCAAFTOTAL settles YES if the two teams collectively score more than the half-point strike (for example over 25.5 for Nebraska vs Illinois) in the game; the title says Full Game but the sampled rules text does not state whether overtime points are included. A postponed game that begins within 48 hours stays open and settles on the official final result; if it does not start within 48 hours the market resolves to a fair price. Rungs are strict greater-than on .5 strikes, so there is no push. KXNCAAFHIGHSCORE (moved here by the reconciliation) settles YES if any Division I game in the 2026 regular season, overtime included, has more than 144.5 combined points; conference championship, bowl and CFP games are excluded, so it is a season maximum over several hundred FBS and FCS game totals.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official final result per the Kalshi wording; the stats provider is not named in the sampled text, so the final score as published by the NCAA or the schools is assumed.
variants_and_edge_cases: Overtime treatment is unstated in the sampled KXNCAAFTOTAL text, whereas KXNCAAFHIGHSCORE says 'including overtime' (and the sibling 4Q total in quarter_and_half_totals says excluding); the Full Game title suggests inclusion but this is not verified.
The sampled rung of 25.5 for a Power-conference game is an extreme low rung of a ladder; the ladder runs from low to high strikes and each rung is a nested event.
Cancelled or non-started games after 48 hours resolve to a fair price, not to NO, so weather cancellations do not pay the under.
Totals have mass at certain sums (3, 6, 7, 10, 13, 14...) so the distance between consecutive .5 rungs carries very different probability.
FBS vs FCS games are included in the series with very high totals possible when a large mismatch occurs.

KXNCAAFHIGHSCORE counts overtime explicitly and spans every Division I game (FBS and FCS, including FCS-FCS games); whether a game between a Division I team and a non-Division I opponent counts as 'a Division I game' is not stated.

Since the 2021 overtime rule (two-point attempts only from the third overtime) long overtimes add about 2-4 points per extra period, so pre-2021 multi-overtime totals overstate today's extreme-total tail for HIGHSCORE.

team_total.label: Team total points
team_total.target: Probability that one team's points exceed a rung.
team_total.mechanism: Team points = own possessions x points per possession against the opponent's defense, constrained by the implied split of game total and spread and by blowout behavior (starters pulled when leading, garbage points when trailing). Team-specific pace, QB, line, red-zone finishing and special teams drive the mean; the distribution depends on style variance. Quotes must be consistent with game total and spread ladders.

inputs.why: Implied team means from lines.
Own opponent-adjusted offensive efficiency determines the team's points per drive.
Opposing defense efficiency (pass versus rush) adjusts the team's expected points.
Own possessions, influenced by own tempo and the opponent's clock usage, scale team points.
Team-specific red-zone TD rate and goal-line approach affects points per trip.
Own kicker quality shapes the 3-point share of points and the key-number clusters.
The team's starting QB status is the dominant driver of its own total and is confirmed late.
Absent receivers or backs lower the scoring ceiling and need replacement-quality estimates.
Own line health shifts sack rate and rushing efficiency and so the scoring rate.
Behavior when leading/trailing.
Weather effects on own scoring depend on the team's pass-heavy or run-heavy style.
Team score residuals show clustering at multiples of 3 and 7 and fat tails.
Sportsbook team totals and implied splits from spread and total provide the benchmark.
Consistency with game total/spread.
Quote history shows when the market absorbs QB, weather and lineup news and benchmarks closing-line value.
Depth and spread determine whether a modeled edge is executable.
Fees reduce edge, especially near 50c where fee per contract peaks.
Volume and open interest signal price reliability and feasible size.
Executed trades reveal real fills and informed flow versus stale quotes.
Open/close/halt and postponement events (including weather delays) define the information set.
Style clash sets how many possessions this offence gets and how explosive they are.
Explosive-pass allowed rate converts directly into this team's points when its quarterback is the strength.
Separates the team's scoring trials from the game's, which the existing pace input (plays per game) does not.
Directly governs the high rungs where a favourite is expected to reach 45+ points.
Ensures the own-score distribution is consistent with game total and spread distributions instead of being fitted separately.
Provides the missing input for the rush-attempt series, whose variance sits in script and sack accounting rather than in scoring.

interactions.hypothesis: Favorite team total x blowout management: when expected to lead big, the favorite's team total is capped by starter removal and clock running; underdog gets garbage points.
Own offense x opponent defense style: pass-heavy offense vs strong secondary is hurt more than vs run defense strength; match style to opponent strengths.
QB and OL availability: unknown QB or OL changes sack rates and efficiency simultaneously, so team total adjustment should combine them.

A strong offence's expected total keeps rising with rating gap only until a three-score lead; beyond that, conservative coaches cut the team's points while persistent coaches keep scoring, so the response to rating gap flattens at a coach-specific level.
interactions.how_to_test: Plot team points versus pre-game gap by persistence tercile and test for a break at gap 21-24.

interactions.hypothesis: A pass-first offence is hurt by a good secondary but not by a good front, and a run-first offence the reverse; the appropriate matchup term is the product of style share with the opposing unit's quality, not the sum of overall offence and defence.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit own points on style share x opposing unit allowed values; compare with additive offence-plus-defence baseline.

interactions.hypothesis: A backup quarterback behind a depleted line loses more than either shock alone, while a healthy line with a backup can still produce points through the run game; the effect is conditional on the other components of the offence.
interactions.how_to_test: Contrast team totals in games with QB change plus OL loss versus QB change alone and OL loss alone.

interactions.hypothesis: Hypothesis, not an established effect: own and opponent points move together through pace but diverge through clock control; the correlation changes sign across regimes, so team total variance cannot be obtained from the game total variance by a fixed fraction.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate correlation of own and opponent points by expected margin and expected pace buckets; confirm sign flip.

interactions.hypothesis: Above a wind threshold a pass-first team's scoring regime switches to short fields and field goals which are also limited by wind, while a run-first team is mostly unaffected; the team total's sensitivity to forecast wind is thus regime-dependent.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare team points in windy versus calm games by pass reliance and kicker range.

nonlinearities.shape: Concave with a cap: team points flatten once the lead exceeds roughly 21
nonlinearities.why: A favourite does not keep scoring proportionally to its rating edge because starters leave and the clock runs; the cap differs by coach, so the high rungs are less probable than a linear rating-to-points map suggests.

nonlinearities.shape: Linear in drives but with threshold at about 9 drives: below that, the team total rarely exceeds mid rungs
nonlinearities.why: A team with few drives needs high efficiency to reach a high rung, and below some drive count the probability collapses faster than the mean implies.

nonlinearities.shape: Sign changes from positive (shootouts) to negative (clock control) across expected-pace regimes
nonlinearities.why: The variance of team points depends on the covariance regime, which alters tail probabilities of high rungs independently of the mean.

mechanism_review.summary: A team's points equal its own drives times points per drive (plus non-offensive scores), where its drives are a share of the game's possessions that depends on the opponent's clock control and turnovers, and where points per drive come from the team's offence against the opponent's defence with a style-dependent split between passing and rushing. The central problem is that the team total is a one-sided slice of a game with a script: a favourite's scoring is capped by blowout management while the underdog's total is lifted by garbage-time drives and constrained by its own offence. The distribution is lumpy (3 and 7 multiples) with a long right tail from short fields and return touchdowns.

stages.name: Own possession count after opponent control
stages.description: The team does not get half the combined drives: the opponent's slow, clock-burning offence trims its chances, turnovers and special-teams plays create asymmetry, and quick scores return possession to the opponent sooner. Own expected drives equal a share of game drives that is estimated from drive-level records rather than from season plays per game.
stages.distribution: Count of own drives, roughly 10 to 14, Gaussian-like with SD of about 1.5; share varies with matchup tempo.

stages.name: Points per drive from offence against defence
stages.description: Own points per drive depend on the opponent-adjusted offence, the opposing defence's pass and rush components, red-zone finishing and kicker range; strengths are not symmetric because a pass-first offence meets only the secondary's quality while a run-first offence meets the front. Late personnel news on quarterback, line and skill players moves this term.
stages.distribution: Per-drive 0/3/7 mixture with team-specific TD share; mean points per drive about 2.0-2.4 for typical FBS offences with wide cross-team spread.

stages.name: Script cap or lift on the team's scoring
stages.description: Once the team leads by three scores the coach substitutes and runs the clock, capping its total; the trailing team passes more and benefits from garbage possessions. Persistence of scoring after a lead is coach-specific and creates a bimodal relationship between rating gap and team total: elite teams vs weak ones either reach 50 or stall at 38.
stages.distribution: Mixture: competitive-game regime (tight, near its mean) versus blowout regime (capped for leaders, lifted for trailers).

stages.name: Conditions and dependence on opponent score
stages.description: Weather affects pass-heavy attacks more, and the relationship between the team's points and the opponent's points (positive via pace, negative via clock control and script) determines the variance of the team total relative to the game total. The ladder must be consistent with the game total and spread distributions.
stages.distribution: Bivariate score distribution with regime-dependent correlation; wind effect threshold-like.

stages.name: Contract mechanics and overtime scope
stages.description: The strike is a half-point greater-than on one team's points and the ladder of rungs is nested, from low teens to the 40s; overtime treatment is not stated. Conditional input set: if overtime counts in KXNCAAFTEAMTOTAL, cfb.ot_model (P(tie after 60 minutes), overtime possession scoring; see the overtime archetype tie curve) adds an increment to the team points distribution; if not, it drops out.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping from the team points pmf to rungs; overtime adds a small mixture component with probability P(tie after regulation).

talent_strength.note: Own offence and opposing defence opponent-adjusted efficiency; broader strength measures are in the catalog but not attached to this archetype.

opponent_matchup.note: Both halves of the opposing defence are attached: secondary coverage for pass-first offences and cfb.run_defense (line yards allowed, stuff rate, rushing PPA allowed) for run-first offences, crossed with the offence style share.

role_personnel.note: Quarterback, receivers and backs, line and kicker.

availability_news.note: Late availability, with the usual absence of an official feed.

coaching_scheme.note: Scheme identity and lead-dependent play calling.

environment.note: Forecast wind and rain applied by team style.

game_context_script.note: Score-state effect on own scoring through starter-removal timing and persistence of scoring by the leader; the benchmark team-total split is removed.

pace_volume.note: Own possessions from tempo and drive share.

distribution_variance.note: Lumpy team-score pmf and its covariance with the opponent; cfb.score_resid (market-derived, WEAK) is removed.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest, lookahead and rivalry/revenge spots can lower or raise a team's scoring intensity but no input in the archetype represents them for team totals; their effect on a single team's points is not quantified.

officiating_rules.note: Crew tendencies change penalty counts marginally and so own scoring by well under a point; the clock-rule regime is a season-level constant that enters via pace, so no officiating input is needed for a team-total rung.

settlement_contract.note: Greater-than half-point strike and the 48-hour postponement rule; overtime scope unresolved and m.ladder_structure (price-derived, BENCHMARK_ONLY) is not an input.

required_data.timestamp_requirement: Completed games before as-of date; ratings as-of the preceding week.
required_data.history_needed: 2014 onward

required_data.dataset: Play-level run/pass and sack accounting
required_data.timestamp_requirement: Plays up to the as-of date; NCAA stat-definition vintage for sacks.
required_data.history_needed: 2014 onward

required_data.dataset: Availability, kicker and weather vintages

required_data.timestamp_requirement: Capture time stamped; use at least 1 hour before kickoff.

contract_review.settlement_definition: KXNCAAFTEAMTOTAL settles YES if the named team scores more than the half-point strike (for example New Mexico over 45.5) in the game; the sampled rules text does not state whether overtime points count. A game postponed but started within 48 hours stays open and settles on the official final result; otherwise a fair price. This archetype holds only KXNCAAFTEAMTOTAL.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official final result of the game per the Kalshi wording; the stats provider is not named in the sampled text.
variants_and_edge_cases: Overtime treatment is not stated in the sampled KXNCAAFTEAMTOTAL text (unlike 4Q and 2H contracts); a team that scores in overtime could cross the strike, and overtime frequency is asserted rather than sourced (to be measured by cfb.ot_model).
Points scored by a team include defensive and special-teams touchdowns and safeties; the sampled text says scores over without exclusion of non-offensive scores.
A very high strike (45.5) for a team belongs to a mismatch or an elite offence and the ladder is nested with rungs down to the low teens.
Cancellation or non-start within 48 hours resolves to a fair price, so weather suspension of an unfinished game is a distinct edge case not covered by the sample.

quarter_and_half_totals.label: Quarter and half totals and team totals
quarter_and_half_totals.target: Probability that points in a quarter/half (game or one team) exceed a rung.
quarter_and_half_totals.mechanism: Period totals = period possessions x points per possession, allocated from the game total by period shares: first-quarter scripted drives and opening possession, end-of-half scoring, second-half tempo and substitution patterns (blowouts), and halftime adjustments. College second-half totals depend heavily on lead size and coach behavior. Short periods have lumpy scoring (0, 3, 7), so exact distribution matters.

inputs.why: Opponent-adjusted period scoring rates give each team's typical profile across quarters and halves.
First-half versus second-half share of scoring, conditional on spread size, is the key allocation parameter.
Implied team points from the game market allocate the expected scoring that periods share.
Opening possession order changes first-quarter and second-half-start scoring chances.
Opening-drive outcomes capture scripted early efficiency for first-quarter totals.
Plays in the period depend on tempo, and tempo differs between early and late periods.
State-dependent pace and pass rate differ by lead and shift period totals.
Second-half starter removal when leading reduces second-half totals for favorites.
Tempo and halftime management.
In short periods, FG chances at end-of-half drives are a material component of scoring.
Weather by period (wind late).
Overtime excluded in period totals; rules.
Period total rungs share information; consistency checks avoid correlated mistakes across thresholds.
A backup quarterback changes the opening script and first-half pace; timestamped confirmation is the point-in-time input.
Opponent-adjusted offence sets expected points per drive in the period.
Opponent-adjusted defence sets the opposing points per drive in the period.
One early turnover decides a quarter; regressing turnover luck separates repeatable offence from noise in 15-minute sample.
Directly produces the mean of every quarter, half and 1H team-total rung from one game-level estimate.
Quarter and half totals need a count of scoring trials inside a short window; this input gives that count and its threshold behaviour.
Gives the exact probability of crossing 6.5 / 7.5 / 13.5 rungs rather than a normal approximation to a lumpy count.
Fourth-quarter and second-half totals diverge from a share-of-total rule precisely in games with large gaps; this input quantifies that divergence.
KXNCAAF2HTOTAL (sampled rung 6.5, text states the 2nd half includes overtime) is shifted and fattened in the right tail by overtime; the other quarter and half totals are not.
KXNCAAF1HTEAMTOTAL needs a team-side allocation of first-half points that does not use any market total split.
KXNCAAFQHIGHSCORE (1/N payout on tied quarters, overtime excluded from Q4) and KXNCAAF1QBTTS, 2QBTTS, 3QBTTS need the joint four-quarter pmf and per-team scoreless mass, not totals or margins.

interactions.hypothesis: Opening possession x first-drive scripts: Q1 totals depend on both who receives and how scripted drives perform.
Lead size x second-half pace: second-half totals fall when a favorite leads by 3 scores; scale by coach behavior.
End-of-half scoring x tempo: fast teams get extra possessions at end of the first half, lifting Q2 totals.

Probability of crossing the 7.5 rung in a quarter jumps when the combined drive count falls from six to four, because with four drives it takes two scoring drives for more than seven points and the zero-scoring mass rises sharply; the effect of tempo is non-linear and strongest for slow-tempo pairings.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate P(quarter total >= 8) by predicted combined drives count and test a break at five drives.

interactions.hypothesis: Fourth-quarter share of the game total depends on the expected gap: when the gap is small, Q4 holds the highest share (two-minute drills, urgency); when large, the leader's rate falls and the trailer's garbage-time scores partially offset, so Q4 share turns down.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate Q4 share by gap bins; compare to the pooled share and fit a piecewise function.

interactions.hypothesis: End-of-half field-goal decisions interact with kicker range: a coach with a reliable kicker takes three points before the half, which raises Q2 and Q4 totals in lumps of three and thickens the pmf at 3 and 10, while an unreliable kicker leads to turnovers on downs and thinner mass at 3.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare the Q2 total pmf by kicker accuracy tercile and decision-aggressiveness tercile.

interactions.hypothesis: Wind that rises in the second half cuts the passing offence's scoring rate and the effect is amplified for fast-tempo pass-heavy offences, so the second-half total responds to the product of forecast wind trend and offensive pass reliance, not to the average forecast.
interactions.how_to_test: Interact forecast wind trend (late minus early) with pass-reliance terciles in a model of 2H and 4Q totals.

interactions.hypothesis: The overtime increment exists only in games tied after regulation, which are close games where starters stay in and the 2H regulation total is least compressed by blowout management; so the increment is not independent of the regulation second-half total and adds right-tail mass exactly where the 6.5 rung is least at risk.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare 2H totals including overtime against regulation 2H totals, split by pre-game absolute margin bins, and test whether adding the increment to a regulation pmf reproduces the empirical 2H distribution.

interactions.hypothesis: Q2 and Q4 gain end-of-half drives and tempo spikes, so in high-total games they are the likeliest argmax, while in low-total games a single touchdown decides the highest quarter and ties among 7-point quarters are common; the drive budget per quarter therefore changes both the argmax probability and the expected tie split.
interactions.how_to_test: By expected-total bin, compare the empirical distribution of the highest-scoring quarter and its tie frequency against the copula simulation and against an independent-quarters simulation.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold at about four combined drives, weak above six
nonlinearities.why: The count of scoring trials is small, so each lost drive removes a large fraction of expected points; the probability of a scoreless period is convex in drive count.

nonlinearities.shape: Point mass at 0 and lumps at 3, 6, 7, 10; survival function is stair-stepped, not smooth
nonlinearities.why: The probability that a quarter total exceeds 7.5 differs by about a third from the probability it exceeds 6.5 because 7 is the most common touchdown outcome; a continuous distribution cannot reproduce that.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise: no effect until lead exceeds about three scores, then offsetting declines and increases
nonlinearities.why: Late leads change who scores and how fast the clock moves only beyond a threshold; below it the quarter looks like a competitive one.

mechanism_review.summary: A period total is the sum of points from both teams in a short window: the number of combined scoring chances (drives that fit in the period, capped by clock) times the probability and size of scores, which come in lumps of 3, 6, 7 and 8, so the distribution is a compound count with a large mass at zero and at the key sums. The mean is a non-uniform share of the game total (end-of-half drives, scripted openers, lead-dependent late periods), while variance is large relative to mean. Overtime matters only for the second half, and for team-total variants only one side's scoring process enters.

stages.name: Game-level scoring expectation allocated to the period
stages.description: A pregame expected total (from opponent-adjusted offences and defences and conditions) is allocated across periods by a share that depends on expected game script: Q2 and Q4 hold two-minute drives and are scored at higher rates per minute, Q1 starts with scripted plays, Q3 starts after halftime adjustments. The share also depends on the gap, since big leads reduce Q4.
stages.distribution: Allocation shares vary around 0.2-0.3 per quarter with game-level dependence; shares are estimated from league history and have sampling noise of a few percentage points.

stages.name: Drive budget inside the period
stages.description: How many drives fit into 15 minutes is set by both teams' seconds per drive, run-pass mix, turnovers and end-of-period truncation; Q2 and Q4 end with abrupt clock stops and sometimes kneel-downs, while Q1 and Q3 usually do not. A slow period of four combined drives caps the total in a way that a mean-based approach hides.
stages.distribution: Count of drives (4 to 7 combined) with threshold effects at low counts; truncation of the last drive at the period end.

stages.name: Points per scoring chance and lumpy scoring
stages.description: Each drive ends in 0, 3, 6, 7 or 8 points with team-specific touchdown-versus-field-goal mix; the period total is the sum of those jumps. End-of-half field-goal decisions, scripted openers and turnovers shift the probability of scoring; kickers matter at the margins because a 3 versus a 0 flips a low rung.
stages.distribution: Compound count with lumps at 3 and 7 and a negative-binomial-like number of scoring drives; overdispersed relative to Poisson.

stages.name: Script and personnel shocks late in the game
stages.description: In Q3 and Q4, lead-dependent behaviour (clock burning, starter removal, garbage-time scoring by the trailing team) reshapes the total; quarterback status and weather change scoring rates in every period but with period-specific timing (wind rising in the second half).
stages.distribution: Conditional mixture: tight totals in competitive games versus bimodal totals in blowouts; discrete shocks from quarterback and weather.

stages.name: Series scope and settlement
stages.description: Series differ in scope: 2H includes overtime, 4Q excludes it, 1H team total counts a single team, and the rung strike lies on the half-point so the settlement threshold is a specific integer of points. The ladder of rungs for one period is a nested family and must be internally consistent.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping from the pmf to rung probabilities; consistency constraint across rungs (monotone survival).

stages.name: Joint four-quarter scoring for highest quarter and both-teams-to-score
stages.description: QHIGHSCORE needs the joint distribution of all four quarter totals, because the payout depends on which quarter is the argmax and on how many quarters tie for it; BTTS needs each team's probability of a scoreless quarter, which is a per-team zero mass rather than a combined total. Quarter totals are positively correlated through game pace and strength, and Q2/Q4 carry end-of-half drives, so treating quarters as independent misprices both the argmax and the tie split.
stages.distribution: Correlated negative-binomial scoring-drive counts per team and quarter with 3/6/7/8 lumps; argmax with N-way tie split; per-team zero mass of roughly a third to a half per quarter.

talent_strength.note: Game-level scoring expectation from offence and defence, allocated by league-baseline shares.

opponent_matchup.note: No input defines how a specific offence matches a specific defence inside a period (for example an opponent that starts slowly or an offence that scripts well), beyond season-level adjusted efficiencies; period matchup structure is unmodelled.

role_personnel.note: Quarterback and kicker identity; backups' snap share in late periods enters via the garbage-time profile.

availability_news.note: Late quarterback status; other availability enters through game-level expectation.

environment.note: Forecast vintage; second-half wind evolution is only partly captured.

pace_volume.note: Combined drive count in the period.

efficiency_conversion.note: Points per scoring drive and field-goal conversion.

distribution_variance.note: Overdispersion, zero mass and lumpy sums. The joint four-quarter pmf covers QHIGHSCORE and BTTS.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest and motivational stakes change the game-level mean slightly but there is no argument they redistribute scoring across periods, and their effect is far below the sampling noise of a single quarter total.

officiating_rules.note: Overtime scope by series and the period-scoring rule definitions.

settlement_contract.note: Overtime scope per series read from the rules text (2H includes overtime, 4Q excludes it); ladder consistency is a benchmark check, not an input.
