contract_review.settlement_definition: Quarter and half total markets (KXNCAAF1QTOTAL, 2QTOTAL, 3QTOTAL, 4QTOTAL, 1HTOTAL, 2HTOTAL) settle YES if the two teams collectively score more than the half-point strike in that period, counting only points in that period; the 2nd half includes overtime (as the 2HTOTAL rules state) and the 4th quarter excludes overtime. KXNCAAF1HTEAMTOTAL settles YES if the named team alone scores over its strike in the first half. Postponed games starting within 48 hours remain open and settle on the official final result; otherwise a fair price. Moved here by the reconciliation: KXNCAAFQHIGHSCORE settles on which quarter has the most combined points (overtime excluded from Q4), paying $1/N to each of N tied quarters; the both-teams-to-score series KXNCAAF1QBTTS, 2QBTTS and 3QBTTS have no listed market and no rules text.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official period scoring from the final box score; Kalshi text says official final result but does not name the stats provider.
variants_and_edge_cases: Period scope by series: 1Q to 3Q and 1H cannot include overtime, 4Q explicitly excludes it, 2H explicitly includes it; the 1HTEAMTOTAL primary text states the scope ('scores over 6.5 points in the 1st half'), what is unstated is how a suspension is handled.

Strike levels in the samples are very low for halves (6.5 for 1H and 2H totals) relative to typical first-half totals (not quantified here: the left-tail frequency of 1H totals of 6 or fewer points must be measured, see cfb.period_total_dispersion validation), so the ladders have many rungs and the sampled rung is one of many nested events.
Safeties, two-point conversions and defensive scores count as points for the team or game; the sampled text does not say otherwise, but extra-point returns are not discussed.
Quarter totals have large mass at 0 and 7, meaning .5 strikes at 6.5 and 7.5 carve very different probabilities (P(total >= 7) versus P(total >= 8)).
A postponed or suspended game starting within 48 hours remains open; a game suspended mid-period (weather) with resumed play affects period labelling and is not addressed.
QHIGHSCORE payouts are fractional on ties (1/N rounded down to the cent), so tied low-scoring quarters (for example two 7-point quarters) split value.
KXNCAAF1QBTTS, 2QBTTS and 3QBTTS are NO_LISTING: whether a safety or a defensive score counts as a team scoring is not read.

quarter_and_half_sides.label: Quarter and half moneyline and spread
quarter_and_half_sides.target: Probability a team leads/wins or covers a spread in a specific half or quarter (period margin, ties per wording).
quarter_and_half_sides.mechanism: Period margin mean is a fraction of the game margin (not proportional): favorites win first halves more reliably because starters and scripted plays dominate early, while second-half margins depend on blowout management, adjustments and depth. Period margin has high variance relative to mean, a large tie mass for quarters, and depends on opening possession and QB/personnel. Settlement of ties (push, no-action or lose) is critical.

inputs.why: Full-game strength prior is the starting point for period margin means.
Adjusted offense differs by period because of scripted openers and depth.
Adjusted defense determines early and late-period suppression.
Team-specific first versus second-half profile determines period margins relative to game margin.
Quarter scoring history by team shows slow starters or strong closers.
Receiving first shifts the first quarter and the order of second-half possessions.
Scripted opening-drive efficiency gives early-period edge.
Second-half behavior of a leading team determines whether the half margin shrinks.
QB identity shifts early scripted efficiency and period margins.
Depth at tails matters in second halves.
Halftime adjustments and tempo.
Period margin residual distribution (with tie mass) is required for spread and ML at periods.
Treatment of ties for period winners (push or loss) and overtime exclusion define settlement.
Quarter and half legs share the game script so period margins are correlated with the game margin; model jointly.
One early turnover decides a quarter; regressing turnover luck separates repeatable offence from noise in 15-minute sample.
Possession count in a quarter is the dominant source of difference between a quarter spread and a share of the game spread.
Q2 and Q4 spreads and highest-scoring-quarter markets depend on these abnormal drives, which are not in a season efficiency rating.
Direct empirical shape for period winner and period spread contracts, whose ties and rung settlement (>7.5) hinge on lattice probabilities.
The same rules text contrast (2H includes OT, 4Q excludes it) changes the target distribution by series; a series-specific spillover makes the difference explicit.

KXNCAAFQHIGHSCORE and KXNCAAF1QBTTS, 2QBTTS, 3QBTTS are live series of this archetype that need the four-quarter joint pmf, per-team scoreless mass and argmax-with-ties payout rather than period margins.
KXNCAAF1HFT settles on a first-half tie plus the full-game (including overtime) winner; the joint needs this conditional, which cfb.corr alone does not measure.

interactions.hypothesis: Talent depth x period: more talented teams win second halves via depth and rotation, so depth matters more in H2 than in Q1.
Opening possession x first-half margin: receiving first adds expected margin to first quarter and shifts half-end possession order.
Blowout behavior x second-half spread: favorites' second-half margins shrink when leading big, requiring conditional distribution on halftime lead.

Expected points in a period equal possessions times scoring rate, so receiving the opening kickoff matters much more for an offence with a high touchdown rate: the extra drive is worth about 0.5 times that team's points per drive, a bigger edge for an elite offence than for a poor one.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress Q1 and Q3 margin on receive-first indicator interacted with team points per drive terciles; compare slopes.

interactions.hypothesis: Hypothesis, not a demonstrated effect: second-half margins depend on halftime state: when the leader is up three scores, depth and rotation determine whether the margin shrinks, grows or stays; below that lead the first-half dynamics persist, so the regime switches at roughly 21 points. The input cfb.blowout_management is itself audited WEAK, so this regime switch is a conjecture to test, not a basis for the model.
interactions.how_to_test: Condition on halftime lead bins and estimate the second-half margin distribution separately for leads above and below 21.

interactions.hypothesis: End-of-half scoring depends on possession order and whether a team plays to score or holds the ball: the team receiving the second-half kickoff has an incentive to hold for a field goal before the half, raising the other team's chance of scoring in Q2.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare Q2 margins when the first-half receiver holds the last possession vs not, split by two-minute efficiency terciles.

interactions.hypothesis: Hypothesis, not a demonstrated effect: a backup quarterback is scripted conservatively in Q1, so Q1 margin shrinks toward zero, but only if the offence's opening script was prepared for him; once the game opens up in later quarters the penalty grows, so the effect of a QB change on period margin depends on the period index.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the margin residual of backup-quarterback games by period; test a monotone increase in the penalty from Q1 to Q4.

interactions.hypothesis: The 2H winner and the full-game winner are strongly dependent through overtime, and 2H sides depend on the 1H result through halftime-lead script; marginal quarters are positively correlated through team strength but only weakly so, which defeats independent-leg pricing.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the empirical correlation matrix of period margins by expected margin bin and test independence on pairs (1H, 2H) and (Q3, Q4).

interactions.hypothesis: The KXNCAAF1HWINNER Tie strike and the two team strikes partition the half-time margin, so their probabilities must sum to one; the tie mass at the half is raised by end-of-half field-goal drives that equalise 7-10 or 14-17 scores and lowered when the team holding the last first-half possession is an efficient two-minute offence, so the three legs move jointly with the end-of-half possession order.
interactions.how_to_test: Tabulate tied halves by whether the trailing team held the last first-half possession and by its two-minute efficiency tercile; check that predicted team and tie legs sum to one and are calibrated.

nonlinearities.shape: Point mass at zero margin plus lumps at 3, 6-8; probability of a margin >= 8 within a quarter is far below a Gaussian prediction
nonlinearities.why: A quarter has only 5-6 combined drives, so margins above 7 require multiple scores; a continuous model misprices tie probability and rung 7.5 by several percentage points.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold near a 21-point lead; weak effect below, strong compression above
nonlinearities.why: Starters stay in until the game is effectively decided; the effect on second-half margin appears only past a lead of about three scores.

nonlinearities.shape: Step function: one extra possession (about 0.5 drive) for the receiving team in Q1 and Q3, none elsewhere
nonlinearities.why: The possession order effect is binary rather than continuous and is concentrated in specific quarters; averaging across periods hides it.

mechanism_review.summary: A quarter or half margin is the difference between two short compound-Poisson scoring processes: the number of possessions each team gets in the period (set by tempo, who received the opening kick, and end-of-half clock behaviour) times the probability that a possession ends in a 3-, 6-, 7- or 8-point score. Period mean margin is a fraction of the game margin, but variance relative to mean is very large and there is a big point mass at zero, so winner markets are trinomial (win, tie, lose), with the tie paying a separate Tie strike in KXNCAAF1HWINNER and neither side elsewhere and spreads sit in a thin lumpy tail. Second-half and fourth-quarter periods are distorted by blowout management and by the contract's overtime scope.

stages.name: Possession order and tempo within the period
stages.description: Each period contains only two or three possessions per team. The team receiving the opening kickoff takes the first quarter's opening drive, and the team that deferred (or kicked off) normally receives the second-half kickoff and so opens the third quarter; deferral is a coach habit. Which team holds the ball at the end of the second quarter depends on the drive sequence, giving a last end-of-half scoring chance. Possession counts differ by period and drive times differ by tempo.
stages.distribution: Small-integer counts (about 2 to 3 per team per quarter) with a deterministic order effect; variance relative to the mean is high.

stages.name: Scoring rate per possession by period
stages.description: Per-possession scoring probability equals the team's opponent-adjusted offence against the opposing defence, but with period-specific modifiers: scripted openers in Q1, end-of-half two-minute drills in Q2, halftime adjustments in Q3, and clock-driven decisions in Q4. Quarter scoring history is mostly noise around the game-level rate.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli outcomes per possession with 3/7 payoff; period-level differences mostly random; real structural effects are a fraction of a point.

stages.name: Availability and the game-level margin prior
stages.description: The game-level expected margin from team ratings and the late quarterback decision supplies the mean from which period means are derived; the translation from game margin to period margin is roughly proportional to the period's share of scoring, but not exactly because favourites score disproportionately in first halves and clock-burn late.
stages.distribution: Gaussian-like prior on game margin scaled by period fraction; period mean about 1/4 (quarter) or 1/2 (half) of game margin, with period noise far exceeding the mean shift.

stages.name: Script effects: blowout management and correlation across periods
stages.description: Second-half and fourth-quarter margins depend on halftime lead: favourites with large leads pull starters and run the ball, compressing their margin, while the first half is played at full strength. Period margins are positively correlated with the game margin and with each other through script and team strength.
stages.distribution: Conditional distribution given halftime lead; correlated joint distribution across periods with sign-flipping mean reversion in blowouts.

stages.name: Period margin lattice and settlement scope
stages.description: The period margin is lumpy: large mass at zero, then 3, 6, 7, with spread rungs at 7.5 needing at least an eight-point period margin. The period winner texts (1Q-4Q, 1H, 2H) say only 'wins the <period>', with no tie clause in the complete text, so a tied period pays neither side; KXNCAAF1HWINNER instead lists a Tie strike that resolves YES on a tied half. The second half includes overtime and the fourth quarter does not.
stages.distribution: Discrete lattice with point mass at 0 (roughly a quarter of quarters for even teams, less for halves) priced explicitly as the Tie leg; series-specific overtime scope.

talent_strength.note: Game-level non-market strength (SP+, PPA, talent) supplies the mean; market ratings are BENCHMARK_ONLY and removed; period conversion is the unresolved piece.

opponent_matchup.note: No input captures period-specific matchups such as a defence that starts slowly against tempo or a team that shows a different formation after halftime; the quarter matchup structure is not defined anywhere in this archetype.

role_personnel.note: Quarterback and starter-removal timing; depth chart effects are not separately defined.

availability_news.note: Quarterback vintage only; other late news enters through the game-level margin.

coaching_scheme.note: Deferral habits, two-minute management and tempo.

environment.note: Weather and venue mostly change full-game scoring level; their period-specific effect (wind late) is second-order against the possession-count noise of a quarter and is not separately modelled here.

game_context_script.note: Lead-dependent behaviour in H2 and possession order in Q1/Q3.

pace_volume.note: Possessions per period for each team.

efficiency_conversion.note: Per-possession scoring in specific period contexts.

distribution_variance.note: Margin lattice and tie mass for the side markets plus cross-period correlation; the four-quarter joint scoring pmf moved with QHIGHSCORE and BTTS to quarter_and_half_totals.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest, rivalry and bowl stakes shift the game-level mean margin but there is no evidence they redistribute scoring across quarters; any such effect is far below the possession-count noise of a 15-minute period.

officiating_rules.note: Overtime scope and tie handling by series are rules facts; targeting-ejection rules matter only for 2H sides, via the game-level model.

settlement_contract.note: 2H includes overtime, 4Q excludes it; KXNCAAF1HWINNER pays a Tie strike while the other winner texts have no tie clause.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Period winner markets (KXNCAAF1H, 1Q, 2Q, 3Q, 4Q, 2H) settle YES if the named team wins the stated period; the complete rules text has no tie clause, so on a tied period neither team 'wins' and both team markets should resolve No (a reading of the text, not stated). KXNCAAF1HWINNER (historical) is a three-way half-time market: 'If the score is tied at the conclusion of the first-half, all team strikes resolve to No and the Tie strike resolves to Yes'. Only points in the stated period count; the 2nd half includes overtime (KXNCAAF2H, KXNCAAF2HSPREAD) and the 4th quarter excludes it. Spread markets (1Q-4Q, 1H, 2H) settle YES if the team wins the period by more than the half-point strike (for example 7.5). Postponement under 48 hours stays open, otherwise a fair price; KXNCAAF1HWINNER stays open for a rescheduled game within two weeks.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official play-by-play and period scoring in the final box score as published by the NCAA or the schools; the sampled text says official final result but not which provider.
variants_and_edge_cases: Tied period: KXNCAAF1H and 1Q-4Q texts (complete in the sample, about 530 characters) contain no tie clause, so a tied period most plausibly resolves both team markets No; KXNCAAF1HWINNER states this explicitly and adds a Tie strike.
Overtime scope differs across series within the archetype: 2H and 2HSPREAD include it, 4Q and 4QSPREAD exclude it, 1H, 1HSPREAD and Q1-Q3 cannot include it.
Two postponement regimes: current series use a 48-hour start window then fair price; the historical KXNCAAF1HWINNER keeps the market open for a game rescheduled within two weeks.
KXNCAAF1H and KXNCAAF1HWINNER both settle on the first-half result but with different tie handling (implicit No versus an explicit Tie strike), so their prices are not interchangeable.

game_stat_props.label: Game and team stat props
game_stat_props.target: Probability that a team or game statistic (yards, turnovers, sacks, TDs, first downs, etc.) meets a threshold per official stat source.
game_stat_props.mechanism: Team/game stats scale with plays and style: yardage by pass/rush split and efficiency, turnovers and sacks by havoc/pressure and ball security, TDs by scoring expectation and red-zone style. The data source and stat definitions (e.g. sack yards counted against rushing, bowl stats, FBS vs FCS) matter for settlement; heavy variance from blowouts and tempo.

inputs.why: Plays scale all counting statistics and differ widely in college tempo.
Pass share determines the split between passing and rushing statistics.
Opponent-adjusted rushing efficiency gives rushing yards per attempt.
Opponent-adjusted passing efficiency gives passing yards and TDs.
Opposing run defense adjusts rushing counts and efficiency.
Opposing secondary adjusts passing yards and explosive passes.
Pass rush against protection determines sacks and pressure-driven incompletions.
Havoc rates predict negative plays, forced fumbles and turnovers.
Takeaway luck regresses; use process measures to project turnover props.
Expected scoring and TD counts.
Game state changes pace and pass rate and thus counting-stat expectations.
Weather shifts pass attempts, completions and kicking statistics.
Distribution shape for team and game stats (blowouts, tempo) determines threshold probabilities.
Stat definition (e.g. whether sack yards count in rushing, FBS-only) and source determine settlement.
Discrepancies between data sources.
Team stats correlate with scoring and script; use joint simulation rather than independent marginals.
A starting receiver or back out redistributes targets and carries; replacement quality sets the stat shift.
Injury news has no reliable official feed in college football, so timing and source matter more than the designation.
Target, carry and snap share translate team volume into player volume; share changes after injuries are the main source of line error.
Receiving yards = completions x yards per completion, and completions scale with dropbacks that depend on score state, so the mean and its spread must be conditioned on expected flow.
The yardage threshold is crossed mostly in games with high snap counts; state-dependent tempo is the mechanism linking expected margin to those counts.
Sets the dispersion of per-completion yards, and so P(325+) relative to the mean.
Links availability of specific pass-catchers to team yardage via formation, instead of treating every receiver as interchangeable.
KXNCAAFTEAMRSHATT counts team rushing attempts, and KXNCAAFTEAMYDS charges sacks and kneels to rushing; both need the script-driven run-play count.
KXNCAAFTEAMYDS settles on total offense = rushing plus receiving yards with sacks and kneels as negative rushing yards, i.e. plays x net yards per play.
Small but rule-specified deduction in KXNCAAFTEAMYDS for the leading team; ignored by gross-yardage models.

interactions.hypothesis: Pace x pass rate: yardage thresholds depend on both plays and mix, and a fast pass-heavy team inflates yards while being penalized by opponent efficiency.
Havoc x turnover luck: takeaway counts should be projected from havoc and pressure with strong regression of realized turnovers.
Spread script x rushing: favorites in lopsided games accumulate rushing yards late, pushing team rushing yards above neutral-situation projections.

A team's dropback response to being a big underdog depends on its own pass-rate slope and tempo: an air-raid, up-tempo offence converts a deficit into many extra pass snaps, while a run-first or slow team under the same deficit still burns clock; so extra receiving yards from the trailing script appear only where pass_rate slope and pace are high.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress dropbacks on the SP+ expected-margin gap interacted with the team neutral pass-rate-over-expected slope and seconds per play; compare the gap coefficient across pass-rate-slope terciles.

interactions.hypothesis: An offence that lives on deep completions has yards per completion multiplied by the opposing safeties' explosive-allowed rate, while a short-pass offence is almost insensitive to it; the product, not the sum, determines the right tail above a high strike.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit yards per completion on depth-of-target x opponent explosive rate and compare to an additive model on held-out games.

interactions.hypothesis: Sustained wind above about 15 mph reduces deep-ball completion and shifts calls to the run, but the cut-in only appears past the threshold and is largest for vertical offences; mild weather has no effect.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare team receiving yards in games with forecast wind above 15 mph against calm games, split by depth-of-target tercile.

interactions.hypothesis: Loss of a top receiver costs more yards in a four-wide scheme (where he is on the field for 90 percent of snaps and targets concentrate) than in a heavy-set scheme where targets spread across tight ends and backs; a backup quarterback shrinks the yards per target of every remaining receiver at once.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the yards-per-attempt drop when a top-2 receiver or the starting quarterback is absent, split by 3+ WR snap-share tercile.

interactions.hypothesis: A team's rushing-touchdown count is its touchdown total times the share credited to runs inside the ten; a designed-run quarterback raises that share, and the effect is largest for offences that reach the red zone often, so the 5+ rushing-touchdown rung depends on the product rather than on either factor.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress team rushing touchdowns on expected touchdowns, goal-to-go run share and quarterback designed-run rate with their product term; compare fit of additive and multiplicative forms.

interactions.hypothesis: Rushing attempts respond to the non-market expected lead with a hinge: below a two-score expected lead the count tracks tempo, above it clock-killing run calls add attempts while total snaps fall, so tempo and expected margin offset each other in heavy favourites.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit attempts on expected margin bins with and without a pace interaction; test a slope change near a 14-point expected margin.

interactions.hypothesis: Under the KXNCAAFTEAMYDS accounting a sack subtracts yards from total offense, so the cost of a sack-prone quarterback scales with dropback volume: a trailing team that passes 45 times loses far more net yards to sacks than a leading team passing 20 times, and the same quarterback pulls total yards down more in chase scripts.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress team total yards residuals on sack rate x dropbacks versus additive sack rate and dropbacks terms; compare held-out error by expected-margin bin.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise: pass share rises about 10 points when trailing by two scores and falls sharply when leading by 21+
nonlinearities.why: Dropback volume is the main driver of the right tail and responds non-linearly to lead size, so a linear score-state term understates both extremes.

nonlinearities.shape: Heavy right tail in yards per completion
nonlinearities.why: A few 50+ yard completions can add 100 yards; threshold probabilities near the mean are sensitive to the tail share of explosive plays rather than the mean yards per attempt.

nonlinearities.shape: Saturating: extra snaps convert into pass attempts at a falling rate as clock-burning kicks in
nonlinearities.why: Beyond about 75 snaps the added plays are disproportionately runs in clock-killing situations, so yards do not scale with tempo one-for-one.

nonlinearities.shape: piecewise-convex in expected margin with hinges near -10 and +14 to +21
nonlinearities.why: Dropbacks rise faster than linearly as the expected deficit grows (trailing teams pass and hurry), and flatten or fall for large favourites that run the clock; the hinge sits in the SP+ margin, not in a second input, so it is a single-input response shape.

nonlinearities.shape: Variance above Poisson that grows with expected touchdowns; fat right tail for 8+ combined
nonlinearities.why: High touchdown rungs are reached in mismatch and shootout regimes where scoring drives cluster, so a Poisson with the right mean understates the tail probability of 8+ total or 5+ team touchdowns.

nonlinearities.shape: Step in expected late lead: near zero when trailing, a fixed few-yard loss once the team is likely to lead at the two-minute mark
nonlinearities.why: A kneel series occurs only when the offence leads with the clock nearly out, so the deduction switches on as P(lead late) crosses roughly one half rather than growing smoothly with margin.

mechanism_review.summary: A team's receiving yards equal its passing-game completions' yardage (excluding 2-point tries), so the outcome is dropbacks x completion rate x yards per completion, truncated by what the game looks like. Dropbacks come from plays in regulation (tempo and possessions) times the pass share, which swings 15 to 20 percentage points with score state; efficiency per attempt depends on the quarterback, receiver depth and opposing pass defence and pressure; the distribution is right-skewed because explosive completions are rare and large. Overtime adds a small right tail (periods 1 and 2 count). Settlement depends on which statistics provider is the source of truth. The reconciliation added touchdown-count series and team rushing attempts: touchdowns are scoring trips times the touchdown (not field-goal) finish rate plus return and turnover touchdowns, split by run/pass at the goal line; the first-touchdown market is a race between two teams' arrival processes with the opening possession as a head start; rushing attempts are plays times a run share that rises with the lead and, under NCAA scoring, includes sacks. Team total yards (KXNCAAFTEAMYDS, re-filed here) are plays times net yards per play, with sack and kneel yardage charged to rushing per the rules note.

stages.name: Snap budget from tempo and possessions
stages.description: The number of offensive snaps a team gets in 60 minutes comes from drives and seconds per snap; both vary with score state and the season's clock rule regime (running clock after first downs since 2023). The budget sets the ceiling for dropbacks, and overtime adds one or two extra possessions with probability under ten percent.
stages.distribution: Roughly Gaussian per-game plays (SD around 9) with heavier right tail in shootouts; overtime adds a discrete lump.

stages.name: Pass share conditional on game script and scheme
stages.description: Out of the snap budget, dropbacks equal plays times the pass rate, which depends on the offence's scheme, quarterback strength, weather and above all expected score state: trailing teams drop back much more, leading ones run. Quarterback scrambles and sacks are dropbacks that do not produce receiving yards, so the relevant count is attempts, not dropbacks.
stages.distribution: Overdispersed count (negative binomial) conditional on expected margin; pass share piecewise in lead size.

stages.name: Completion rate and yardage per completion
stages.description: Each attempt becomes a completion with probability set by the quarterback, protection against the opposing pressure rate, receiver quality and coverage; the yards per completion are air yards plus yards after catch, with a long tail for explosive plays. The opposing secondary's explosive-allowed rate acts multiplicatively on a deep-passing offence.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli completions with heavy-tailed positive yards per completion; team receiving yards skew right (median below mean).

stages.name: Pass-catcher and quarterback availability
stages.description: The effective passing unit depends on who plays quarterback and which receivers are available; with sparse college injury reporting these shocks arrive late. A missing receiver shifts targets to replacements, lowering yards per target more than the number of targets; a quarterback change lowers both completion rate and yards per attempt and widens uncertainty.
stages.distribution: Discrete availability states with replacement-quality uncertainty; effect size is a mixture, not a smooth shift.

stages.name: Dispersion and joint script correlation
stages.description: The final yardage is a sum of a correlated set of components (plays, pass share, yards per attempt) that move together with the game script: a shootout lifts all three. The tail above a high rung such as 325 is dominated by those correlated high-script games, so independent marginals understate it.
stages.distribution: Right-skewed, correlated mixture; the threshold probability is a tail quantity sensitive to variance and covariance.

stages.name: Settlement and stat-source reconciliation
stages.description: Yards in overtime periods 1 and 2 count and 2-point yards do not; the official provider may differ from public box scores, so labels and live checks must use the same definition. A postponement beyond 48 hours resolves to a fair price rather than a win or loss.
stages.distribution: Deterministic given the provider; risk comes from definitional mismatches of a few yards near the strike.

stages.name: Touchdown counts and the first-touchdown race
stages.description: For the TEAMTD, TOTALTD, RSHTD, RECTD, DSTTD and FIRSTTDTEAM series the count is drives that reach scoring range times the share finished with six points, so a team that stalls into field goals has the same points but fewer touchdowns. Goal-line play calling and a running quarterback decide the rushing versus receiving credit; interceptions, fumbles and kick returns create defensive and special-teams touchdowns that count for totals, the first-touchdown race and DSTTD but never for rushing or receiving counts. The receiving team of the opening kickoff gets the first chance in the race, and overtime touchdowns settle a race left open after regulation.
stages.distribution: Overdispersed (negative-binomial) touchdown counts with variance growing in expected scoring; rare-event Poisson for return touchdowns; competing hazards with a head start and a small no-touchdown mass for the race.

stages.name: Team rushing attempts under expected game script
stages.description: KXNCAAFTEAMRSHATT has no listed market, so its definition is unread; under NCAA statistics a rushing attempt includes designed runs, scrambles, sacks and kneel-downs, so the count equals snaps times run share plus sacks taken. Run share rises sharply when protecting a lead and falls when chasing, which makes the attempt count a mirror image of the dropback count used for receiving yards and strongly dependent on the non-market expected margin.
stages.distribution: Approximately Gaussian count per game (SD of several attempts) with a lead-dependent mean; piecewise in expected margin.

stages.name: Team total offense: plays times net yards per play
stages.description: KXNCAAFTEAMYDS (SMU 475+) settles on rushing plus receiving yards, with sack and kneel yardage charged to rushing. Total yards are the snap budget times net yards per play, where the run/pass split comes from the expected script, a sack-prone quarterback lowers net yards on dropbacks, and a late-leading team gives back yards on kneels. Explosive plays create a right tail, and a big favourite reaches high rungs early and then runs clock, so the right tail is truncated by blowout management.
stages.distribution: Approximately normal team yardage (SD near 100 yards) with right skew from explosive plays and a lead-dependent truncation; overtime periods one and two add a small lump.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest, travel and rivalry effects on passing volume are not defined for this contract; the effect is probably small but nothing in the archetype lets it be tested.

officiating_rules.note: Crew penalty rates change drive length marginally; the one rule that matters for yardage, the clock rule regime, is inside cfb.state_dependent_pace, so no separate officiating input applies to a team receiving-yards total.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Nine team/game stat series. KXNCAAFTEAMRECYDS settles YES if the named team records at least N receiving yards (325+ = strike 324.5) and KXNCAAFTEAMYDS if it records at least N total yards of offense (475+), where total yards = rushing plus receiving yards and sacks and quarterback kneels are negative rushing yards; yards in the first or second overtime count and 2-point conversions do not. Touchdown-count series: KXNCAAFTEAMTD (team touchdowns), KXNCAAFTOTALTD (both teams), KXNCAAFTEAMRSHTD and TEAMRECTD (rushing/receiving touchdowns; a teammate's fumble-recovery touchdown is not credited), KXNCAAFDSTTD (at least one defensive or special-teams touchdown by either team); overtime touchdowns count and 2-point conversions never do. KXNCAAFFIRSTTDTEAM settles on the team scoring the first touchdown of any kind, overtime included, with a separate 'No team scores a TD' outcome. KXNCAAFTEAMRSHATT (team rushing attempts) is TITLE_ONLY with no listed market. Postponement under 48 hours stays open; otherwise a fair price. No statistics provider is named.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official game statistics per the Kalshi wording (official final result); the specific provider (NCAA stats, conference, ESPN or Sportradar) is not named in the sampled rules, so reconciliation against CFBD box scores is required before using it for labels.
variants_and_edge_cases: Nine series share the archetype after reconciliation: team receiving yards, team total yards, five touchdown-count series (team, total, rushing, receiving, defensive/special teams), the first-touchdown race and team rushing attempts; their volume drivers differ (dropbacks, plays, scoring trips, return chances, run plays).
Overtime period 1 and 2 yards count; from the third overtime the format is alternating 2-point attempts whose yards are excluded, so the rule has an effect only for very long games.

Receiving yards can be negative on a catch behind the line; whether negative receiving yards net against the total, whether sacks or laterals affect it, and whether team receiving yards equal completions' yards under official NCAA statistics are NOT stated in the sampled text; this is domain knowledge only and the definition is SOURCE_UNVERIFIED.
Threshold rungs are .5 strikes written as N+ (for example 325+), so there is no push; the ladder of rungs for one team and game is a monotone survival curve.
Postponement of more than 48 hours or cancellation resolves to a fair price rather than void.

Overtime wording differs: RECYDS and DSTTD say 'first or second overtime periods', TEAMTD, TOTALTD, RSHTD and RECTD say 'overtime'; since the third overtime onward consists of two-point attempts that never count, the two wordings are equivalent in effect.
KXNCAAFTEAMTD counts touchdowns 'recorded by' the team; whether a defensive or special-teams touchdown scored by that team counts is not stated (TOTALTD and FIRSTTDTEAM state all touchdowns count).

KXNCAAFTEAMRSHATT is TITLE_ONLY (no listed market, no rules text), so whether sacks and kneel-downs are rushing attempts (they are under NCAA statistics) and whether overtime attempts count is not read.
FIRSTTDTEAM has a 'No team scores a TD' outcome covering regulation plus overtime, a small point mass for very low-total games.
KXNCAAFTEAMYDS overtime wording ('first or second overtime periods') matches RECYDS; its sampled secondary text is cut at 600 characters, so any clause after the postponement sentence is unseen.

overtime.label: Overtime occurrence and overtime length
overtime.target: Probability that the game goes to overtime (and potentially to multiple overtimes) as defined in the contract.
overtime.mechanism: Overtime occurs when regulation ends tied: probability = mass of the final-margin distribution at exactly zero, which is concentrated in close spreads and kicker-driven scoring, and sensitive to the lattice of college scoring (3, 6, 7, 8) and late-game decisions (kneel, go-for-it, field goal at end). Rule mechanics (25-yard start, alternating possessions, 2-point attempts from later periods) determine length and extra-period markets. Market wording must define overtime as an extra period played.

inputs.why: Mass at zero margin conditioned on spread and total.
Expected scoring, with lower scoring raising tie mass.
Small rating gap lifts overtime probability.
Overtime rules, number of periods, 2-pt rule.
Kicker-driven scoring clusters on 3s.
End-of-regulation decisions (kneel, take a tie).
Possessions: fewer possessions raises tie variance.
Low-scoring conditions raise tie chance.
Reduces tie chance for large favorites.
Contract definition and any restrictions.
Realized overtime frequency for calibration.
Tie incidence is the entire target of KXNCAAFOT and the entry condition for KXNCAAFMOSTOT; direct estimation from non-market axes avoids circularity with the price.
The existing coaching input measures tenure and scheme but not the one decision that converts a close game into overtime.
Sets the conditional probability of a second and later overtime period, which compounds geometrically into the 9+ period contract.
Only the rule regime of OT 3+ makes 9+ periods possible, and its per-period tie probability depends on exactly this quantity.
Turns a per-game tail probability into the season contract and handles the monotone state variable (record already set).

interactions.hypothesis: Spread near zero x low total: overtime probability peaks for evenly matched, low-scoring games and is nearly flat for large spreads.
Coach end-of-game decisions x kicker: teams that settle for a tie-breaking or tying FG vs go for win change overtime odds in the final minutes.
Pace x variance: fewer possessions increase the share of games within a score at the end, boosting tie probability.

Tie probability depends jointly on the absolute rating gap and the margin SD, which in turn depends on possessions and weather; at a gap of zero the probability rises as SD falls, but at a gap of seven it rises with SD, so the sign of the SD effect flips with the gap.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit tie probability on gap, SD proxy and their product; contrast the SD slope in gap<3 versus gap>7 games.

interactions.hypothesis: A coach who habitually kicks the tying field goal creates overtime only if his kicker is accurate from 35-45 yards; a poor kicker makes the decision pointless, so incidence of created ties depends on the product of intent and capability.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare tie rates in games where the trailing team had a late tying-FG opportunity by decision-profile tercile x kicker accuracy tercile.

interactions.hypothesis: The probability that a period ends tied switches regime at the third overtime from a score-matching process (0.25-0.35) to a two-point match (about 0.5), so survival to 9 periods multiplies a small early factor by a roughly 0.5^6 tail; both the regime and the number of games enter the season probability.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate period-tie rates separately for OT1-2 and OT3+ from historical long games; compare the geometric prediction with the observed count of 6+ OT games.

interactions.hypothesis: Overtime ties are more likely when both offences are poor from the 25 or both kickers are reliable (both score a field goal), and wind lowers touchdown probability while leaving short field goals reachable; the period tie probability is a product-sum of both teams' scoring distributions.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute predicted period tie probability from team distributions and evaluate calibration against realised OT1 outcomes by weather bucket.

nonlinearities.shape: Gaussian-like decay in absolute rating gap with a long thin tail; flat near zero gap
nonlinearities.why: A gap of 10 points has about one third of the tie probability of a gap of 3, but not zero because of volatile late scoring, so a linear gap term misprices both ends.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise with regime break at overtime period 3; period tie probability bounded near 0.5
nonlinearities.why: Because p_a p_b + (1 - p_a)(1 - p_b) stays between about 0.45 and 0.55 for all realistic rates, the probability of long overtimes is insensitive to team quality but very sensitive to the number of periods.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex in games remaining: 1-(1-q)^N is nearly linear for tiny q and saturating only at very large N
nonlinearities.why: The market price should decay almost linearly as games complete, then jump to 1 if a qualifying game happens; a smooth hazard model misrepresents the step.

mechanism_review.summary: Overtime happens if and only if the game is tied after four quarters, so P(OT) is the point mass of the regulation margin distribution at exactly zero: roughly the margin density at zero (large when teams are evenly matched and the total is low) adjusted for the scoring lattice, plus an excess created by late-game decisions to tie rather than win. How many periods follow is a separate renewal process: each period from the 25-yard line ends tied only if both teams score the same, with a rule change at the third overtime to alternating two-point attempts, so the count of periods is nearly geometric and the 9+ strike is a long-tail event across hundreds of games in the season.

stages.name: Regulation margin distribution near zero
stages.description: The final regulation margin has centre equal to the expected rating gap and spread equal to the sum of game-level noise and rating uncertainty; the tie probability is the mass at exactly zero, which falls roughly Gaussianly with the absolute gap and is highest when the gap is within three points. Fewer possessions or lower totals reduce the margin SD and therefore raise the mass at zero for close matchups.
stages.distribution: Point mass of a discrete lattice, approximately density at 0 times lattice factor; peaks at zero gap and decays like exp(-gap^2/(2 sigma^2)).

stages.name: Scoring lattice and low-scoring conditions
stages.description: Points arrive as 3, 6, 7 and 8 (and occasionally 2), so some margins are far more reachable than others; field-goal-heavy games produce ties more easily because both teams accumulate multiples of three. Wind and rain make scoring lower and lumpier, and kickers with limited range convert drives to threes.
stages.distribution: Lumpy discrete distribution with elevated mass on margins reachable by equal numbers of three-point scores; weather lowers the total and raises lumpiness.

stages.name: End-of-regulation decisions that create or avoid ties
stages.description: In the last two minutes the team trailing by three can kick the tying field goal, a team trailing by eight needs a touchdown and a two-point conversion, and a team with the ball in a tie may kneel into overtime. These choices put extra mass at zero relative to a smooth margin density and differ by coach.
stages.distribution: Binary decisions at specific score and clock states; excess mass at tie created by coach-specific decision rules.

stages.name: Overtime period renewal process
stages.description: Once in overtime, each period gives each team a possession from the 25-yard line; the period is tied if both score the same number of points (both touchdown with equal conversion, both field goal, both none). Scoring probabilities per possession are far higher than ordinary drives, so a tie after period one is the exception, giving a decay by period with a modest per-period continuation probability.
stages.distribution: Geometric-like renewal with continuation probability depending on team scoring rates, roughly a quarter to a third per period in early periods (to be fitted).

stages.name: Rule regime change and season-extreme aggregation
stages.description: From the third overtime periods are single alternating two-point attempts, so each period ends tied only if both succeed or both fail, near one half; reaching nine periods requires six consecutive such ties after two ordinary overtimes. Across several hundred games the contract is a rare-event union, so exposure (games remaining, maximum already seen) matters as much as per-game probability.
stages.distribution: Piecewise geometric survival with a regime break at period 3; season-level union probability 1-(1-q)^N for a very small q.

talent_strength.note: Only the absolute non-market rating gap (SP+ or own rating) matters for the tie curve; market ratings are BENCHMARK_ONLY and removed from the input list.

opponent_matchup.note: Overtime incidence depends on the margin distribution and on both teams' scoring rates from the 25, which is carried by ot_possession_scoring_rate; no separate matchup structure beyond those rates is justified for an event decided by margin equal to zero.

role_personnel.note: Kicker quality drives tying field goals and OT field-goal outcomes; quarterback and others enter through expected margin.

availability_news.note: Availability matters only through the margin mean, margin SD and expected total that feed the tie curve (a quarterback change or late scratch widens the SD and lowers the total); cfb.qb_status_pit is wired into stage s1 through the expected-margin inputs.

distribution_variance.note: Point mass at zero margin on the scoring lattice, set by the regulation tie curve and possession-count variance.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest, rivalry and standings stakes alter the margin mean slightly but do not specifically produce ties; the incremental effect would be below the sampling noise of roughly fifty overtime games a year.

contract_review.settlement_definition: KXNCAAFOT settles YES if at least one overtime period is played in the named game (strike 1); an overtime period counts as played once it commences, via a legal snap in the first two overtimes or a first two-point attempt from the third overtime onward, and once started counts in full whether or not both teams get a possession. KXNCAAFMOSTOT settles YES if any Division I game in the 2026 regular season goes to at least 9 overtime periods. A game postponed but started within 48 hours stays open and uses the official final result; outside that window the markets resolve to a fair price.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official game records (final box score with periods) as reported by the NCAA or the participating schools; Kalshi text does not name a provider for these two series.
variants_and_edge_cases: KXNCAAFOT is equivalent to regulation tie; KXNCAAFMOSTOT is an aggregate over all Division I games with a rule-regime change at the third overtime (alternating two-point attempts), so the per-period survival is not constant.
A period counts as played once started even if the game ends on the first snap of that period, so a sudden-death result in period k still counts k periods.
Overtime periods scheduled but never started do not count, which matters only for weather suspensions or ties after curfew; the rules do not say how a suspended overtime is treated.

KXNCAAFMOSTOT primary text scopes the market to 'the 2026 college football regular season', and the sibling HIGHSCORE rules state conference championship, bowl and CFP games are not part of the regular season, so conference championship games are reasonably excluded; the sampled MOSTOT text is truncated and how a game halted by weather during overtime counts is still not addressed.
The 9+ strike is greater-or-equal on count of periods; a 9-overtime game with the ninth period commenced counts, even if the ninth ends the game on the first snap.

touchdown_scorer.label: Touchdown scorer markets (anytime and first)
touchdown_scorer.target: Probability that a named player scores a touchdown (anytime or first) under contract definition.
touchdown_scorer.mechanism: Player TD probability = team expected TDs x player share of scoring opportunities (goal-line carries, red-zone targets, QB rushing), adjusted for blowout removal and availability, with first-TD adding the probability the team scores first. College features: wide variation in team scoring, QB rushing TDs, goal-line specialists, heavy rotation and garbage-time TDs by backups.

inputs.why: Role-based scoring rates convert team TDs to player probabilities.
Expected team TDs derived from implied totals are the scoring pool.
Red-zone and goal-line share distinguishes scorers from yardage accumulators.
QB rushing TDs and sneaks take scoring opportunities from backs and receivers.
Starter removal and backup TDs.
Teammate absences redistribute goal-line and red-zone usage.
Depth chart clarity and recent changes show who holds the goal-line role.
First-possession probability shifts first-TD team odds.
Opening-drive TD rates inform first-TD markets.
Opposing defense's red-zone and position-specific weakness modulates scoring odds.
Early exits (injury, blowout) remove scoring opportunities from starters.
What counts (offensive TDs only?).
Suspended or ejected players (targeting) are removed from scoring chances and shift shares to teammates.
New transfers often take goal-line or receiving roles, changing historical share-based scoring rates.
Quote history shows when the market absorbs QB, weather and lineup news and benchmarks closing-line value.
Depth and spread determine whether a modeled edge is executable.
Fees reduce edge, especially near 50c where fee per contract peaks.
Volume and open interest signal price reliability and feasible size.
Executed trades reveal real fills and informed flow versus stale quotes.
Open/close/halt and postponement events (including weather delays) define the information set.
Converts efficiency into the count variable the live contracts settle on, and separates rushing from receiving touchdowns.
Controls the rushing versus receiving touchdown split: KXNCAAFTEAMRSHTD (5+) and TEAMRECTD (1+) are functions of this mix.
The first-TD market needs the order of arrival of two Bernoulli processes, not a count, and has an explicit No TD outcome.
Direct input for KXNCAAFDSTTD and a component of the first-TD and total-TD markets.
Gives tail probabilities for high-count rungs where a continuous model fails.

interactions.hypothesis: Team TD pool x role share: share depends on the expected game script; trailing teams pass more near goal line, shifting TD probability from RBs to WRs.
QB mobility x goal-line carries: mobile QBs absorb TDs, lowering RB scoring odds even with high red-zone volume.
Blowout x depth: in lopsided games backups score late, raising anytime TD for backups and lowering for starters pulled early.

Team rushing touchdowns equal TD count times rushing share, and the rushing share is higher with a mobile quarterback and a power-run goal-line mix; both the count and the share vary across teams, so the product has more spread than either factor.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit rushing TD counts with an interaction of expected TDs and goal-line run share; compare with an additive version.

interactions.hypothesis: In a one-sided game the leading team runs near the goal line and uses backups, raising the rushing share and total TD count for the leader, while the trailing team throws and adds receiving touchdowns; the combined effect on high-count tails depends on the gap.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare rushing and receiving TD counts by gap bin and leader/trailer role.

interactions.hypothesis: First-TD probability depends on the receiving team's head start and each team's early hazard, and defensive touchdowns add a third arrival channel that can reverse the order when the opposing offence is turnover-prone; the three are not independent because the same offence both scores and turns over.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate P(first TD by team) as a function of opening possession and turnover-proneness; test the interaction of receive-first with pick-six rate.

interactions.hypothesis: A defensive or special-teams touchdown flips the game script, and the knock-on effect on the opponent's passing and rushing touchdown counts depends on the pre-game expected margin: it is large in an evenly matched game where the scorer's lead changes the trailing team's play mix, and small when the scorer is already a heavy favourite or the opponent is far behind anyway.
interactions.how_to_test: Using SP+ expected margin bins, compare rushing and receiving touchdown counts of the team that conceded a DST touchdown against those in games without one, and test whether the gap shrinks as the absolute expected margin grows.

nonlinearities.shape: Heavy right tail: variance exceeds Poisson mean and grows with expected total
nonlinearities.why: The probability of 8 or more touchdowns is several times the Poisson value at the same mean because high-scoring teams cluster in shootouts and mismatches.

nonlinearities.shape: Head-start step for the receiving team plus a small point mass at no touchdown
nonlinearities.why: The opening possession order gives a discrete advantage that cannot be represented by a smooth rate, and some games have no touchdown at all.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise in lead size: run share rises sharply beyond a 14-point lead
nonlinearities.why: Leading teams run in short yardage and burn clock, so the type split is sensitive to the lead once it is two scores.

mechanism_review.summary: Touchdown counts equal the number of scoring trips times the probability each trip ends in a six-point score, plus non-offensive touchdowns (the game_stat_props rules texts include them for total and first-touchdown counts; the team-count text is silent), split into rushing, receiving and returns by goal-line play calling and turnover returns. Scoring trips follow possessions and efficiency (the same machinery as team and game totals), but the live contracts settle on counts of touchdowns and not points, so finishing (touchdown versus field goal) is the central variable. First-touchdown markets are a race between two arrival processes with a head start for the receiving team, and counts above the mean live in a heavy tail created by mismatches and shootouts. Reconciliation note: the archetype currently has no live series; the team/game touchdown series were reassigned to game_stat_props, which reuses these inputs.

stages.name: Scoring trips and touchdown conversion
stages.description: A team produces scoring trips (first downs inside the opponent 40) in proportion to its possessions and efficiency against the opposing defence; each trip ends in a touchdown with probability set by goal-line efficiency, play calling and kicker alternatives. Touchdown count rather than points is the quantity, so a field-goal-heavy offence has the same points but fewer touchdowns.
stages.distribution: Binomial or compound count of touchdowns per trip with overdispersion across teams and games.

stages.name: Touchdown type: rushing versus receiving
stages.description: Close-range plays favour runs and quarterback sneaks, longer scores favour receiving; the split depends on the offence's scheme, quarterback mobility and score state (leaders run, trailers pass). Backups and depth-chart roles change who scores but only marginally change the team's rushing count, and the fumble-credit rules decide edge cases.
stages.distribution: Multinomial split of touchdowns by type with team-specific share; shares shift with lead size.

stages.name: Race for the first touchdown
stages.description: The first team to score a touchdown is determined by the order in which two hazard processes first fire; the opening possession order, scripted opening drives and defensive scores matter, and there is a probability that neither team scores in the full game. For a future named-player first-scorer market, whether overtime touchdowns count is unread; the sibling team race (KXNCAAFFIRSTTDTEAM, now in game_stat_props) counts them.
stages.distribution: Competing hazards with a deterministic head start for the opening receiver; a small point mass of no-touchdown games.

stages.name: Defensive and special-teams touchdowns
stages.description: Return touchdowns require opposing turnovers or kick-return opportunities and are rare, partly skill (ball-hawking defences, return specialists) and partly luck, with rule changes on kickoffs altering exposure. They add to totals and race markets but are excluded from the rushing and receiving counts.
stages.distribution: Rare-event Poisson with small rate (game probability of at least one on the order of 15 to 25 percent, to be fitted).

stages.name: Count dispersion, availability and settlement
stages.description: High-count rungs (total TDs of 8 or more, rushing TDs of 5 or more) are tail events where clustering in mismatches fattens the distribution; late availability and eligibility news affect team strength rather than the count directly. No live series here: the two-point and overtime treatment of the sibling team-count texts in game_stat_props is not assumed for a future player market.
stages.distribution: Negative binomial with dispersion that increases in expected total and gap; tail sensitivity to blowouts.

talent_strength.note: Team scoring efficiency at the touchdown level plus non-market opponent-adjusted strength (SP+, PPA) now attached; the benchmark team_total_split is removed.

opponent_matchup.note: Opposing defence TD per trip allowed by type and overall opponent-adjusted defence; cfb.dvp (named-position matchup, WEAK) removed.

role_personnel.note: Mobile quarterback and skill-player availability for the rushing/receiving type split; depth_chart and player_usage (WEAK, named-player only) removed.

availability_news.note: Quarterback status (the main news item) and skill-player absence shift the trip count and type shares; suspension_eligibility (WEAK) removed.

coaching_scheme.note: Goal-line play calling and scripted openers.

environment.note: Wind and rain (cfb.weather_pit) shift the run/pass touchdown split and the count; the size of the effect is unquantified (weather_effect_on_td_split).

game_context_script.note: Lead-dependent run share and opening possession.

pace_volume.note: Expected scoring trips = possessions (cfb.pace, cfb.drives) x trip rate; cfb.td_per_scoring_trip supplies only the per-trip conversion, so the volume side is measured by the attached pace and drives inputs.

efficiency_conversion.note: TD conversion and type, plus non-offensive scores.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest, rivalry and bowl stakes shift scoring slightly but there is no argument that they change touchdown-specific outcomes beyond the game-level scoring mean, so no separate input is justified for TD counts.

officiating_rules.note: Settlement rules for two-point conversions, fumble credit and overtime; targeting and other penalties are second-order.

settlement_contract.note: Counts exclude two-point tries, overtime touchdowns count in periods 1-2, race market includes defensive scores.

fields: touchdown type (rush, pass, interception return, fumble return, kick return, blocked kick)

contract_review.settlement_definition: After the market-universe reconciliation no live series is filed under touchdown_scorer: the six team and game touchdown series previously here (TEAMTD, TOTALTD, TEAMRSHTD, TEAMRECTD, DSTTD, FIRSTTDTEAM) were assigned to game_stat_props, whose record now carries their settlement reading. A named-player anytime or first-touchdown-scorer contract would settle on official scoring credit, but no such contract text exists to read, so no settlement detail is asserted.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official game statistics and scoring summaries of the final result; Kalshi text refers to numbers recorded by the team during the game and names no provider in the sampled rules.
variants_and_edge_cases: No live series: the team/game touchdown counts and the first-team race were reassigned to game_stat_props; the mechanism and inputs below remain as the catalog definition for a future named-player scorer market and are reused by game_stat_props stage s7.
A future named-player market would need its own reading of fumble-recovery credit, overtime and the treatment of a player who does not play (void versus No), none of which can be read now.
Two-point conversions never count in any sampled sibling touchdown series, including in overtime; a player market could differ.

season_futures.label: Season-level events (conference, playoff, title, awards)
season_futures.target: Probability of a season-level college event (conference title, playoff berth/seed, national title, final ranking, award).
season_futures.mechanism: Simulate the season with uncertainty in team strength, unbalanced schedules, conference tiebreakers and the selection process; priors from market ratings and roster continuity; selection by committee adds a behavioural layer modelled from past rankings. Awards add narrative and ballot timing. Cross-market coherence constrains the set and exposes stale quotes.

inputs.why: Conference race simulation with tiebreakers links team ratings to title game and berth odds.
Format and seeding rules in force define how strength converts to playoff and title probabilities.
Strength prior with uncertainty is the base for all season simulations.
Composite ratings provide an independent check on strength.
Returning production determines how much last-season results carry over in preseason priors.
Talent composite gives the ceiling and depth used for preseason priors and late-season durability.
Unbalanced schedule difficulty changes expected wins and playoff-resume quality.
Luck-adjusted records give truer strength than raw wins for resume and ranking projections.
Ranking dynamics and committee behavior translate results into playoff selection.
QB injuries or changes drive contenders' title odds.
Award markets depend on narrative and team success more than on pure production.
Linked futures must satisfy sum-to-one and implication constraints; violations flag stale quotes.
Sportsbook futures prices provide benchmark probabilities after de-vig.
Contract definitions of eligibility, cancelled games and the ranking source resolve edge cases.
Portal churn is the main driver of preseason rating changes and futures priors.
Quote history shows when the market absorbs QB, weather and lineup news and benchmarks closing-line value.
Depth and spread determine whether a modeled edge is executable.
Fees reduce edge, especially near 50c where fee per contract peaks.
Volume and open interest signal price reliability and feasible size.
Executed trades reveal real fills and informed flow versus stale quotes.
Open/close/halt and postponement events (including weather delays) define the information set.
Season outcomes are order statistics over a schedule; the simulated distribution, not the point rating, prices playoff and conference markets.
Win-total, undefeated, home-undefeated, head-to-head wins and conference-title contracts all reduce to this vector plus rules.
Correlated uncertainty is the main reason conference win-count markets and champion probabilities are fatter-tailed than independent-game simulations.
The contracts on playoff, quarterfinal, semifinal, seed and conference representation are selection outcomes whose mapping from results is committee-specific.
Conference champion, qualifier and top-finisher markets depend on structure, and the 2026 season contains markets for conferences with changed membership.
Only a multi-season strength process with program inputs can price long-dated qualification contracts.
Supplies the injury-driven fat tails to team strength draws used in all season-level contracts.

KXNCAAFBOWLGAME (sampled WYO, rules text: selected to play in a bowl game or the CFP, regardless of whether they actually compete; only NCAA-certified Division I bowls count) needs eligibility and slot-balance logic that no win-total or title model supplies.
KXNCAAFCS, KXNCAAFFCS, KXNCAAFD3 and KXNCAAFIVY are TITLE_ONLY outright markets on divisions and a conference that the FBS-centred inputs do not cover.

KXNCAAFSECWINS, BIGTENWINS, BIG12WINS and ACCWINS (rungs 8+, 7+, 5+, 4+ teams with 10+ regular-season wins) need a joint conference-grid simulation in which every intra-conference game hands one team a win and the other a loss.
Prices the KXNCAAFCFPCONF count rungs, where slot competition and the conference-champion bid rule dominate.
KXNCAAFCONFMATCHUP and KXNCAAFLSUTEX2X settle on compound events whose legs are strongly dependent.

interactions.hypothesis: Committee preferences x results: berth probability depends on the quality of wins and strength-of-record language; losses late weigh more than early.
Schedule x conference tiebreakers: remaining head-to-head games determine tiebreakers non-linearly.
QB injury risk x top-heavy contenders: title odds concentrate in teams with a single dominant QB, so injury scenarios dominate variance.

Playoff berth probability is a steep step in the number of losses: a team with zero or one loss is very likely in, a team with three losses rarely, and which side of the step the team lands on depends on who the losses came against and when; the committee's treatment of one loss also depends on conference championship status.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate P(berth) by loss count and quality of losses on historical committee years; fit a step with conference champion and loss-timing interactions.

interactions.hypothesis: A contender's title odds are a mixture over quarterback health states: with the starter its rating is high, with the backup it falls several points, and the draws shared across games produce fat tails; top-heavy contenders (one dominant quarterback) have more mass in the downside branch.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate title odds with and without the hazard, and test whether realised outcomes of teams with elite QBs show larger deviations from rating-implied expectations.

interactions.hypothesis: Conference championship qualification depends on unbalanced schedules and head-to-head tiebreakers: a team that has already beaten its closest rival holds the tiebreaker and needs fewer wins, so remaining head-to-head games have asymmetric value that a simple expected-wins model misses.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare conference qualifier probabilities from a full tiebreaker simulation against a ranking by expected wins on historical seasons.

interactions.hypothesis: Over a four-year horizon the contribution of current talent decays toward a program mean while portal and revenue resources renew it; the incremental value of an extra recruiting-class point is large in year one and small by year four.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit multi-season rating AR(1) with recruiting and portal covariates and test the lag structure of their coefficients.

interactions.hypothesis: Selection rules differ between seasons (field size, automatic bids for champions, seed construction) so the same resume gives different berth probability under different formats; contracts for the same season must use the format regime in force, and the 24-team expansion market implies a possible future regime.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit berth probability separately by regime and test if pooling across formats worsens calibration.

interactions.hypothesis: For KXNCAAFLSUTEX2X the regular-season result changes the second leg: an LSU win lifts LSU's CFP odds and lowers Texas's, and the two must then land in opposite bracket halves; the probability of the rematch final conditional on the first result is far from the unconditional rematch probability, so the product of marginals misprices it.
interactions.how_to_test: In the season simulation, compare P(rematch final | LSU wins on Nov 14) with P(rematch final) and with the independence product.

nonlinearities.shape: Product structure: P(undefeated) = prod p_i; small per-game changes compound exponentially
nonlinearities.why: A team with 85 percent win probability in each of 12 games has a 14 percent chance of an undefeated season but at 90 percent it is 28 percent; the market price must reflect compounding, not averaging.

nonlinearities.shape: Steep logistic in loss count with a conference-champion shift
nonlinearities.why: Berth probability falls from near certainty at 0-1 losses to a small fraction at 3, and a shifted threshold for champions of strong conferences.

nonlinearities.shape: Positive skew in aggregate win-count variance from correlated draws
nonlinearities.why: The variance of the total of wins across a conference is greater than the sum of independent game variances because of shared rating uncertainty, producing fat tails in count markets.

mechanism_review.summary: Season-level outcomes are functions of the whole schedule and of several layers of rules: team strengths are uncertain and correlated draws (with shocks from quarterback injury), each game is a noisy contest whose probability depends on site, rest and matchup, regular-season wins determine conference standings through unbalanced schedules and tiebreakers, conference champions and ranked teams are selected by committee into a bracket whose size and seeding rules vary by season, and long-dated contracts add a random walk of program strength. Settlement wording (regular season only, selection not participation, ties paid to all) changes which function of the simulation is the target.

stages.name: Team-strength prior with correlated uncertainty
stages.description: Start-of-season ratings combine last year's performance regressed by returning production, recruiting talent and portal changes; the uncertainty is large (several points) and shared across a team's games, and connectivity is thin across conferences. In-season, ratings update by results, but the same posterior draw affects every remaining game, which creates correlation that drives the tails of win-count contracts.
stages.distribution: Latent Gaussian rating vector with prior SD 5-6 points, shrinking with games; joint posterior with positive correlation across a team's games.

stages.name: Quarterback and key-player shocks
stages.description: Single-player availability alters a contender's rating by several points; the probability of the starting quarterback missing at least one regular-season game is large enough to matter, and the replacement quality varies widely. These shocks generate the heavy lower tail of team strength and lower the favourite's title concentration.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli per game with heavy-tailed rating impact; mixture over games missed.

stages.name: Schedule path and game outcomes
stages.description: Each remaining game has a win probability from the rating difference, home-field edge and rest; the regular season win count is a Poisson-binomial with correlated draws, and special counts (undefeated, home-undefeated, head-to-head wins) are products or comparisons of these. Unbalanced conference schedules matter because teams in the same conference do not play each other equally. The conference 10-win count series add a second layer: the number of teams over a threshold depends on the whole conference grid, where every intra-conference game hands one team a win and the other a loss, plus a shared conference-strength shock, so cfb.conf_schedule_win_dependence simulates the grid jointly.
stages.distribution: Poisson-binomial (correlated) counts; undefeated probabilities are products of per-game probabilities so tiny differences compound.

stages.name: Conference standings, tiebreakers and title game
stages.description: Conference records determine standings; ties are broken by head-to-head, common opponents and other conference-specific rules, which are nonlinear in the remaining schedule. The title game pairs the top teams under the season's format; the champion is the winner of that game or the top team under the format, and a tied top-N finish pays every tied team.
stages.distribution: Discrete order statistics with tiebreaker thresholds; probabilities depend on small differences in head-to-head results.

stages.name: Committee selection and bracket path
stages.description: The CFP committee ranks teams by resume rather than by rating; conference champions and a seeding rule determine who enters the bracket and where; rank moves slowly week to week and is sensitive to who loses to whom. Berth, seed, quarterfinal, semifinal and finalist probabilities are bracket-path products and depend on the format in force that season. SEED and TOPSEED settle on the exact seed assigned (for example #12, or a top-4 seed), so the seeding rule in force (champion-protected versus straight seeding by ranking) changes which teams can occupy a seed.
stages.distribution: Ordinal selection with inertia; bracket progression product of conditional win probabilities with seed-dependent opponents.

stages.name: Multi-year horizon and cross-contract coherence
stages.description: Long-dated contracts such as qualifying before 2030 require a multi-season random walk of program strength with coach exits and recruiting momentum; all futures are linked by shared draws, so probabilities across contracts must be coherent. Settlement wording choices (regular season only, ties) determine which function of the draws is evaluated.
stages.distribution: AR(1)-type mean reversion of team strength across seasons; union probability over four seasons.

stages.name: Bowl eligibility and selection
stages.description: KXNCAAFBOWLGAME is settled on selection, not participation: a team needs 6 wins (or an APR-ranked 5-7 fallback when eligible teams fall short of slots), then competes for its conference tie-in slots, with the CFP taking top teams first and bowl committees choosing the remainder; the contract list of eligible bowls excludes FCS playoffs. Eligibility detail missing from cfb.bowl_selection_state: under NCAA bowl rules only one win over an FCS opponent counts toward the six (to be verified for 2026), and teams that lose a conference title game can finish 6-7, so the threshold is on countable wins, not raw wins.
stages.distribution: Threshold event on a win count (>=6) combined with a slot-shortage regime; bubble teams (5-7 to 6-6) carry the probability mass while 8-win teams are near-certain.

stages.name: Lower-division and Ivy champion mechanics
stages.description: FCS, D3 and Ivy League champion markets are filed here but follow different formats: FCS has a seeded playoff bracket, D3 a larger bracket, and the Ivy League has no championship game and decides the title on conference record with possible shared titles; each needs division-specific ratings rather than SP+.
stages.distribution: Single-elimination bracket survival for FCS and D3; a conference-record race with ties for the Ivy League.

stages.name: Compound events: title-game pairs, rematches and conference counts in the CFP
stages.description: Several futures settle on joint outcomes rather than one team's path: KXNCAAFCONFMATCHUP pays when a named pair secures both title-game slots (resolving at qualification, not when played); KXNCAAFLSUTEX2X needs LSU to beat Texas in the regular season and again in the national final specifically; KXNCAAFCFPCONF counts Group of Six teams in the field; KXNCAAFCONF asks whether the champion comes from a given conference. Each must be read off one season simulation that preserves the dependence between legs.
stages.distribution: Joint events from a correlated simulation; rare compound events (rematch-final) with probabilities of a few percent and large Monte Carlo relative error.

talent_strength.note: Preseason and in-season ratings with correlated uncertainty plus a multi-year trajectory.

opponent_matchup.note: Season-level outcomes aggregate dozens of games, so unit-level matchups are second-order relative to schedule composition and rating uncertainty; matchup effects are absorbed into game win probabilities in the schedule vector.

role_personnel.note: Quarterback identity and replacement quality; other positions are not separately modelled for season contracts.

availability_news.note: Injury hazard and portal/eligibility events; no official injury feed exists.

coaching_scheme.note: Coach quality and coaching changes affect multi-year program strength and in-season stability, but no input defines coach effects separately from team ratings for futures; the program trajectory index only includes tenure and contract status.

environment.note: Weather and venue effects act per game and wash out over a season-long schedule except for the home-field component, which is carried in game win probabilities through the site term.

game_context_script.note: In-game script matters for margins but season contracts depend on win/loss only, so score-state effects do not enter beyond the game win probability; scoring margin affects only ratings.

pace_volume.note: Pace and possession counts determine per-game scores, not season outcomes directly; the count of games is fixed by the schedule and counted without volume.

efficiency_conversion.note: Efficiency enters through opponent-adjusted ratings and luck-adjusted records.

distribution_variance.note: Correlated rating draws and the Poisson-binomial distribution of wins; the simulation output (season_sim_distribution) is WEAK as an input and futures_coherence is BENCHMARK_ONLY, both removed.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Schedule path, bye and rest, and committee behaviour.

officiating_rules.note: Format, tiebreaker and title-game rules are the rule layer.

settlement_contract.note: Regular-season-only counts, selection not participation, ties paid to all, neutral exclusion and multi-year window.
