contract_review.settlement_definition: Season futures settle on resolved season results. Win totals (KXNCAAFWINS, 12+ wins) count official regular-season games only and 'Ties do not count as wins'; UNDEFEATED counts regular-season games only; UNDEFEATEDHOME counts games at the official home stadium (neutral sites excluded); H2HWINS compares two teams' regular-season wins with a Tie outcome when equal; the conference count series (SECWINS, BIGTENWINS, BIG12WINS, ACCWINS) settle YES if at least N conference teams win 10+ regular-season games. Conference champion series (SEC, ACC, B10, B12, AAC, MAC, MWC, SBELT, CUSA, PAC12) settle on winning the 2026 conference championship game and qualifier series on qualifying for it; CONFMATCHUP resolves when the named pair secures the title-game slots; REGTOP top-5 finishes count all teams tied on conference record as achieving the position. CFP series settle on qualifying (PLAYOFF), reaching the quarterfinals, semifinals or final (QF, SF, FINALIST), winning (KXNCAAF), seed (#12 SEED, top-4 TOPSEED), Group of Six count (CFPCONF, Pac-12 included), champion's conference (CONF) and the LSU-Texas double (LSUTEX2X: regular-season win and a national-final win over Texas). BOWLGAME settles on selection to an NCAA-certified bowl or the CFP (FCS playoffs excluded); TFUT on CFP qualification after issuance and before 2030-31; FCS, CS and D3 on winning the respective national championship. KXNCAAFBACC, BSEC, BB10, BB12, IVY and PAC10 are TITLE_ONLY.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official NCAA, conference and CFP committee results (final standings, official conference championship result, CFP selection show); the Kalshi text cites Source Agencies for some markets but names no provider for win counts.
variants_and_edge_cases: The archetype contains single-season counts (WINS, UNDEFEATED), conference structure events (SEC/ACC/B12/B10/MAC/AAC... champion and qualifier), selection outcomes (BOWLGAME, PLAYOFF, QF, SF, FINALIST, SEED, TOPSEED, CFPCONF), a multi-year event (TFUT before 2030) and a combination event (KXNCAAFLSUTEX2X: LSU beats Texas in the regular season and beats Texas again in the national championship game specifically).
Selection-versus-participation: BOWLGAME settles on being selected, whereas PLAYOFF and QF depend on committee selection and format rules that differ by season (number of teams, auto bids, seeding).
Regular-season top-N finish markets pay all tied teams, a ties rule that makes probabilities sum above one across teams.

Six series are TITLE_ONLY with no rules text: KXNCAAFBACC, BSEC, BB10, BB12 (older duplicates of conference champion tickers), KXNCAAFIVY (the Ivy League has no championship game) and KXNCAAFPAC10 (defunct conference name).
Realignment: the Pac-12 champion and qualifier markets in 2026 imply a reconstituted conference with new members and game formats not in historical data.

Conference 10-win count series count all regular-season wins (an FCS win counts) and exclude the conference title game; head-to-head games between conference members make the teams' win counts negatively dependent.

KXNCAAFCS and KXNCAAFD3 are historical 2025-26 FCS and Division III champion texts ('wins the 2025-26 College Football FCS National Championship'); KXNCAAFFCS is the 2026-27 FCS series, so the same event is listed under two tickers across seasons.
H2HWINS counts total regular-season wins even if the two teams play different numbers of games, so an extra scheduled game (Hawaii rule, a replacement game) changes the comparison.

awards_and_honors.label: College football awards (Heisman and conference awards)
awards_and_honors.target: Winner of a voted individual award.
awards_and_honors.mechanism: Voted awards follow production percentile, team success and narrative; quarterbacks on top teams dominate and late-season prime-time games weigh more. The distribution across candidates, not a single mean, prices the market, and vote clustering by region and position matters.

inputs.why: Narrative and production to date.
Historical vote-share distribution.
Usage and volume determine the production totals voters actually see for each candidate.
Passing efficiency for quarterbacks.
Quarterback status (injury, benching) can end a candidacy abruptly, so confirmed availability is a hard filter.
Rushing production adds to quarterback narrative.
Touchdown rates by role translate usage into the headline numbers voters weight most.
Team success and CFP position.
Schedule strength discounts production.
Turns the current leaderboard and projected remaining production into probabilities for the order-statistic contract.
Controls how often a leader candidate drops out of the race or resolves No, directly shaping probabilities for later-season rungs.
Replaces the unmeasurable narrative input by features voters can observe, separately per award.
Coach of the Year (KXNCAAFCOTY) is decided on surprise relative to expectation, which no other input measures.
Directly models the decision process behind the draft-declaration series rather than treating it as an award.
The four AP Defensive Player of the Year series and the sack/TFL leader series need defender production and pass-rush usage, which the offence-centric inputs do not carry.

interactions.hypothesis: Team rank multiplies a candidate's production in voter perception.
Efficiency against weak schedules is discounted by voters.
Quarterback status changes the candidate's late-season production.

An award candidate's chance is the product of leading the visible production race and staying healthy: a candidate with a small production lead and high workload faces a higher chance of falling behind because of injury, so the joint of current gap, workload and hazard shapes the probability more than the gap alone.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate the production race with and without the hazard and compare to realised award outcomes of past candidates by workload tercile.

interactions.hypothesis: Voters weight statistics by team success and discount production against weak schedules, so a candidate's effective support is production percentile times a team-rank factor times a schedule discount; the same stats on a ranked team and an unranked team yield very different vote shares.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit logit vote share with the product of stat percentile and team rank; compare with additive features.

interactions.hypothesis: Hypothesis to test: a coach who beats expectation by many wins wins only if the team also finishes ranked or wins a title; above a threshold of wins above expectation the probability jumps, and below it conference rank decides.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate winner probability by bins of wins above expectation crossed with final rank across history.

interactions.hypothesis: For the AP conference Defensive Player of the Year, voters reward sack and tackle-for-loss leaders much more when the player's team is ranked or contending; a high pass-rush production rate on a losing team converts to fewer votes, so the production effect is conditional on team record.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit historical conference DPOY winners on sack/TFL rank, team win percentage and their product; test whether the production slope rises with team record.

interactions.hypothesis: Remaining schedule changes a candidate's projected production before the ballot, and for a receiver it also depends on whether his starting quarterback keeps playing; a Biletnikoff candidate with an easy remaining schedule gains only if his team keeps passing at the same rate.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare realised production in remaining games with projections split by remaining opponent rank and team pass rate.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex in the gap: probability of overtaking falls rapidly once the lead exceeds about one game's production
nonlinearities.why: Remaining games contribute a bounded amount of production, so a lead above the remaining capacity is effectively decisive, making probabilities approach 0 and 1 faster than a linear lead model.

nonlinearities.shape: Winner-take-all concentration: vote share to winner probability is a steep softmax, not proportional
nonlinearities.why: A candidate with 40 percent share of expected votes wins far more than 40 percent of the time because winner-take-all amplifies leads.

nonlinearities.shape: Heavy-tailed: a small probability of immediate elimination with large impact, increasing in workload
nonlinearities.why: Season-ending injuries remove a candidate abruptly; the probability is small per game but compounds across the remaining games and concentrates in the highest-workload players.

mechanism_review.summary: The archetype covers voted awards decided by electorates responding to visible statistics and team success (AP conference awards, national position awards such as the Biletnikoff), finalist selection by award bodies, and a coach-of-the-year decision rewarding overperformance against expectation. Each player contract is filtered by participation (no play resolves No), then by projected production against the remaining schedule up to the ballot date, then by the electorate's weighting of production, team success and visibility; co-winners split the payout. Statistical-leader and draft-declaration series were moved out by the reconciliation.

stages.name: Candidate pool and participation
stages.description: Only players who play contribute; the candidate pool for a voted player award is the few dozen high-production receivers (Biletnikoff) or edge rushers and linebackers (AP Defensive Player of the Year), with injury and benching hazard removing some each week. A candidate who misses games loses visible production and one who sits out the season resolves No, so participation is the first filter for every player series.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli participation per game with fat-tailed season-ending probability; heavier for high-workload positions.

stages.name: Production accumulation that voters see
stages.description: Voted awards respond to visible season production: receiving yards and touchdowns for the Biletnikoff, sacks, tackles for loss and takeaways for the AP Defensive Player of the Year. A candidate's end-of-ballot totals come from per-game usage times efficiency against the remaining schedule and the games left before the ballot, so the projected production race among a handful of candidates shapes the vote, with teammates competing for the same volume.
stages.distribution: Sums of overdispersed per-game counts; maximum of correlated sums; ties possible.

stages.name: Electorate response for voted awards
stages.description: Voters see counting statistics, team record and ranking, and highlights, and award ballots are collected at a fixed date before bowls; electorates differ by award (AP voters for conference awards, a committee for position awards), and positional constraints (receiver for Biletnikoff) filter candidates. Vote share is a multinomial contest with winner-take-all payoff and ties when shared.
stages.distribution: Multinomial vote shares with concentration; winner-take-all contest; ballot date fixes the information set.

stages.name: Coach of the Year outcome
stages.description: Coach of the Year is awarded for exceeding expectation: wins against a preseason non-market expectation, ranking gains and conference outcomes. The ballot is a decision by an electorate, not an output of a game model, so the surprise index and the information available at the ballot date matter more than final strength.
stages.distribution: Logistic winner probability driven by a single latent surprise score with a winner-take-all contest among a few coaches.

stages.name: Settlement mechanics and procedural risk
stages.description: Co-winners pay 1/N, a player who does not play in the season resolves No, and finalist markets resolve No if finalists are not reported before the winner; ballots close before bowls, so postseason production is irrelevant, and an inactive market can stop trading before results are known.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping with discrete tie fractions; procedural risk is a small probability mass.

talent_strength.note: Team success and coach expectation drive votes; individual player talent enters through production.

role_personnel.note: Usage determines volume; quarterback status matters only through a receiver's targets and team success for coach votes.

availability_news.note: Injury, benching and transfer hazard; no official feed exists.

coaching_scheme.note: Coach of the Year; scheme shifts to usage are not separately defined.

environment.note: Venue and weather affect individual game production but over a season-long cumulative stat these wash out except through the opponent-adjusted per-game rates; no separate environmental input is justified.

game_context_script.note: Score-state effects (trailing teams pass more, leading teams run and rotate) change award candidates' cumulative production but no input models the script effect on a candidate's usage; its size relative to injury hazard is unknown.

efficiency_conversion.note: Per-game production per opportunity for receiver candidates (inside leader_race_state, used here as the projected award-ballot production race) and sack, TFL and pressure rates per pass-rush snap for defensive awards; the offence-only WEAK inputs are removed.

officiating_rules.note: Officials do not affect award voting or season totals except through statistical corrections; the relevant rules clauses (tie, participation) are carried under settlement_contract, not as an officiating input.

settlement_contract.note: Tie-sharing, participation and finalist-announcement clauses read from rules.

required_data.dataset: Player game logs and season statistics
required_data.timestamp_requirement: Completed games before the as-of date; stat corrections timestamped. Snapshot weekly and store the vintage; leader markets settle on recorded regular-season totals, so keep the final official figure separately from the running CFBD sums (official figures can differ by tens of yards); conference membership must be as-of the contract season.
required_data.history_needed: 2013 onward for award features; 2005 onward for leader projections

candidate_sources.name: CollegeFootballData.com API
candidate_sources.note: Player season stats and some game stats (game-level coverage SOURCE_UNVERIFIED)

fields: candidates with vote share where public
required_data.timestamp_requirement: Official announcements; ballot date fixed per award.
required_data.history_needed: 2005 onward

candidate_sources.name: Award organisation websites and Associated Press
candidate_sources.note: Winners and finalists; vote totals only for some awards (Heisman)

required_data.dataset: Team schedule, ratings and remaining opponents
required_data.timestamp_requirement: As-of the last completed week.
required_data.history_needed: 2005 onward

required_data.dataset: Injury, transfer and participation news
required_data.timestamp_requirement: Capture time stamped; usable only if captured before the contract's decision time.
required_data.history_needed: Self-capture forward

contract_review.settlement_definition: Voted-award series settle YES if the named person wins the award in the stated season: AP conference awards (KXNCAAFACCAWARD, BIG12AWARD, BIGTENAWARD, SECAWARD; the samples are Defensive Player of the Year), national awards (KXNCAAFAWARD, sampled Biletnikoff) and the Bear Bryant Coach of the Year (KXNCAAFCOTY). For player awards, a player who does not play in the season for any reason resolves No, and if several players share the award YES pays 1/N rounded down. Finalist markets (KXNCAAFAWARDFIN) settle YES if the player is selected as a finalist as reported by a Source Agency, and all resolve No if finalists are not announced before the winner. The COTY text states no tie or participation clause. Statistical-leader series moved to unreg:season_stat_leader and KXNCAAFDRAFTDECLARE to coaching_and_governance_events.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Award bodies' official announcements and Associated Press results for voted awards; finalist lists as reported by Kalshi's Source Agencies.
variants_and_edge_cases: Four mechanisms share the archetype: AP-voted conference awards (four conferences), national position awards selected by award bodies (Biletnikoff sampled), finalist selection, and coach of the year.
The sampled AP conference Defensive Player of the Year series have status inactive in the evidence, so trading can lapse before the ballot is known.
Player award texts resolve No when the player does not play in the season for any reason, and pay 1/N to co-winners; the COTY text has neither clause.
Finalist markets resolve No for everyone if no finalist list is reported by a Source Agency before the winner announcement.
KXNCAAFAWARD carries an award code per event (BILE sampled); other national awards (possibly Heisman) may be listed under the same series with different electorates, which the sample does not show.

polls_and_cfp_rankings.label: College football AP poll and CFP ranking markets
polls_and_cfp_rankings.target: A team's rank (or being in the top N, or the number of distinct #1 teams) in the AP poll or CFP rankings on a stated date.
polls_and_cfp_rankings.mechanism: Rank follows results, strength of schedule and voter behaviour: a win over a ranked team raises rank, an upset loss by a favourite drops it far more than the same loss by an underdog, and rankings carry inertia. Distinct-#1 markets are driven by the upset probability of the few top teams. The dated release (week or committee reveal) fixes the information set.

inputs.why: Voter inertia and loss penalties determine how rank responds to each result.
Result-based composite ratings predict the results that move rank (hybrid: build from results only).
Conference standings and CFP position define who is eligible for top ranks.
Remaining and past schedule strength set both loss risk and resume credit.
Offensive efficiency feeds game win probabilities.
Defensive efficiency feeds game win probabilities.
Cross-conference calibration decides how a conference's wins are valued.
Rivalry and bowl stakes change upset risk.
Quarterback availability changes win probability in top games.
Playoff format rules decide what the CFP committee must rank.
Models the voter response layer that turns results into ranks for every AP contract in this archetype.
Needed for successor-given-loss in churn and any-week-number-one contracts.
Structural model for the two number-one contracts (APANY and APCHURN) where history is too thin for frequencies alone.
Provides the committee-specific mapping that differs from AP voting and from ratings.
Handles boundary markets where individual strength is not the main driver.
A settlement-mapping input that determines which ranking is evaluated.
KXNCAAFAPRANK (Final AP #1) and late-season KXNCAAFAPANY/APCHURN paths cannot be priced without a title-probability input; the machinery otherwise lives only in season_futures.

interactions.hypothesis: A loss costs less rank when the opponent was highly ranked or the schedule was hard.
Ratings translate to rank only through conference-title and tiebreak outcomes.
Committee ranking rules differ from AP voting, so the same results produce different top-N sets.

The rank penalty of a loss is larger for a higher-ranked team and smaller when the loss came against a highly ranked opponent or a hard schedule, so the drop is the product of rank, opponent rank and timing; the same loss moves a number-three team five places and a number-fifteen team only two.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate drop size by previous rank, opponent rank and week; check multiplicative structure against additive in a held-out set of seasons. Test it as terms on rank, opponent rank and week in a model, not on the transition model own coefficients.

interactions.hypothesis: When the leader loses, the successor probability depends on first-place vote distribution and on whether the number two team also won; a split ballot raises the chance that a third team becomes number one, which adds to the distinct count.
interactions.how_to_test: Tabulate handovers by first-place-vote gap and by number two's result in past seasons.

interactions.hypothesis: Committee rankings before conference championships treat unbeaten and one-loss teams one way, and after champions are decided the champion status resets the order; so the same resume yields different ranks before and after the title games, and the Nov 24 release comes before the championships.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit rank models separately before and after championship week; compare weights on the champion indicator.

interactions.hypothesis: Entry to the AP top 25 saturates quickly in vote points: once a team has votes comparable to rank 25 a single win moves it in, but far below the line even a big upset win leaves it out; the effect of a win is concentrated in teams near the line and depends on conference credit.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate P(enter) by distance from the line in points and by conference, for teams that won as underdogs.

interactions.hypothesis: Head-to-head games between top teams make losses perfectly negatively correlated and guarantee that at least one of the top teams loses, so the count of distinct number-ones is not a sum of independent losses; the schedule structure of the top eight teams matters.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate churn with and without head-to-head constraints and compare to observed distinct counts.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex in previous rank for loss penalties and asymmetric: losses cost more than wins gain
nonlinearities.why: A loss by the top team can drop it several places while an equivalent win moves it up only if teams above lose, making rank changes skewed and dependent on the starting rank.

nonlinearities.shape: Bounded per-week hazard (about 5-20 percent) compounding over 13 weeks into a high-probability of at least one change
nonlinearities.why: Weekly upsets of the number one are rare but accumulate, so the distinct count distribution is Poisson-like with mean around 3 to 5 across the season, not a linear function of rating.

nonlinearities.shape: Probit-like in the vote-point gap to rank 25
nonlinearities.why: Probability of being ranked changes quickly only within a narrow band around the cut line; far from the line the probability is nearly 0 or 1.

mechanism_review.summary: A rank is the output of a voting body reacting to results and perception, not of team strength directly. AP voters begin from last week's ballot and move teams by asymmetric amounts: a loss by a highly ranked team costs more than the same loss by a lower-ranked team, an upset win by an unranked team earns entry only if it clears the boundary, and the preseason ballot is built from last season and returning production. The CFP committee builds a resume ranking with explicit factors (strength of record, wins over ranked teams, conference title, head-to-head and injuries) but also moves slowly. Distinct number-one counts are governed by upsets of the few top teams and the succession rule, while boundary contracts (top 25, exactly #25) depend on the density of similar teams near the cut line.

stages.name: Results of the games that move the ballots
stages.description: Rank changes follow the outcomes of weekend games, so the first stage is the win probability of each ranked or near-ranked team in each game, with margin and venue; unlikely wins by lower-rated teams create the large changes, and top teams' head-to-head games guarantee a swap.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli outcomes with game win probabilities between 50 and 99 percent for top teams; correlated through shared rating uncertainty.

stages.name: Voter response: inertia and asymmetric movement
stages.description: Given results, voters adjust the previous ballot: top teams that win usually stay, losses drop a team by an amount that depends on its rank, the opponent's rank and the timing in the season, and unranked teams enter only after wins over ranked or similar teams. Preseason polls reflect hype and returning production, and the final poll reflects bowl and playoff results.
stages.distribution: Ordered-response with strong persistence; asymmetric (drop larger than rise) and convex in rank.

stages.name: Succession at number one and ballot state
stages.description: When the number one loses, the successor depends on how first-place votes and points are distributed among the next teams; the count of distinct number-ones is a counting process over losses by the leader and successors, and head-to-head games and the preseason order set the starting state.
stages.distribution: Markov chain over a small set of contenders; counting process with rare events (3-8 per season).

stages.name: Committee resume ranking
stages.description: The CFP committee ranks teams from resume and results, with explicit weights on strength of record, quality wins, losses, conference championship and head-to-head; rankings start in early November and change weekly with strong inertia. Exact rank markets need the whole ordering around the target position, particularly where teams have similar resumes.
stages.distribution: Ordinal with inertia and local reshuffling; uncertainty greatest in the middle and at rank 25.

stages.name: Boundary density and release mapping
stages.description: Entry into the top 25 and exact-rank contracts are decided near the cut line where vote points differ by small amounts; the evaluated release is determined by a calendar and a label map, with a fallback to the next published release if none carries the date.
stages.distribution: Gaussian-like vote-point noise around a threshold; deterministic label mapping.

stages.name: Postseason results and the Final AP #1
stages.description: The Final AP poll is released after the CFP championship game, so KXNCAAFAPRANK on the Final #1 is driven by bowl and CFP results: who wins the national title, with a small tail where voters rank another team first; the same bracket results feed the late-season number-one handovers that APANY and APCHURN count.
stages.distribution: Single-elimination bracket survival then a near-deterministic link from champion to AP #1 with a small split-ballot tail.

talent_strength.note: Team strength drives game win probabilities; rating is not rank.

opponent_matchup.note: Specific upcoming opponents and quality of wins already earned.

role_personnel.note: Quarterback availability in top games; other personnel enter through ratings.

availability_news.note: Committee explicitly considers key injuries; AP voters react to injury news.

coaching_scheme.note: Coaching and scheme matter only through game outcomes, which are already in ratings; no input specific to coaches affects how voters rank a team, so none is justified here.

environment.note: Weather and venue affect individual games' win probabilities but the poll contracts depend on results and voting behaviour; environment is accounted for in the game win probability via site only.

game_context_script.note: The weekend result and margin trigger rank moves; the succession chain is a dynamic process.

pace_volume.note: There are no counts of plays or possessions in a poll contract; volume does not enter beyond margin of victory in game results.

efficiency_conversion.note: Efficiency per play enters only through game win probabilities and is already carried by ratings; no separate per-play conversion input applies to voting outcomes.

distribution_variance.note: Vote-point noise near the cut line and heavy-tail upsets of top teams.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Conference standing and resume schedule strength; cfb.motivation (WEAK) is removed.

officiating_rules.note: Committee protocol and format; AP voting procedures are not formal rules.

settlement_contract.note: Official AP website and CFP release labelled by date with a fallback rule.

candidate_sources.note: Official source of truth for the contracts

required_data.timestamp_requirement: Timestamped; usable only if before the release date.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Poll contracts settle on a specific labelled ranking release: KXNCAAFTOPAPRANK on whether the team is ranked in the AP top 25 at a given week (for example Week 5), KXNCAAFAPRANK on the exact rank in the AP Final Rankings (expected Jan 26, 2027), KXNCAAFAPANY on being ranked number one in any eligible AP poll of the season starting with the Preseason poll, KXNCAAFAPCHURN on at least N distinct teams ranked number one in any poll including Preseason and Final, and KXNCAAFCFPPOLL and TOPCFPPOLL on exact or top-N rank in the CFP rankings of a labelled date (for example Nov 24), falling to the next published CFP rankings after that date if none is labelled then. Resolution is determined solely by the official AP website or the CFP rankings.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official AP Top 25 poll as published on the Associated Press website and official CFP rankings; Kalshi text names these sources explicitly.
variants_and_edge_cases: Two bodies with different processes share the archetype: the AP poll of about 60 voters each week and the 13-member CFP committee, which begins weekly rankings late in the season, so the number of releases before a date differs.
The KXNCAAFCFPPOLL sampled rules text contains an unfilled template token (|| Time Period ||) in place of the season, a text defect that suggests template variables may not always be filled in.
KXNCAAFAPCHURN counts all polls including Preseason and Final; APANY covers any poll starting with the Preseason poll; both depend on the number of polls and on AP's label conventions.
Exactly #25 on a CFP release is a boundary event; the top 4 market depends on the committee's top four, and seeding rules do not change the ranking list.
Statuses vary: TOPAPRANK sample is finalized, CFPPOLL inactive; markets can be closed or settled before the contract is read, so state matters.

KXNCAAFAPRANK resolves on the AP Final Rankings expected Jan 26, 2027, after the CFP championship game, so bowl and CFP results are part of the information set and the final #1 is tied to the national champion.

team_event_counting_specials.label: College football team and event counting specials
team_event_counting_specials.target: A team or game count (turnovers gained, sacks, interceptions, field goals, two-point conversions) or a rare event (weather delay) relative to a threshold.
team_event_counting_specials.mechanism: Team counts are plays times a rate: turnovers and sacks follow opponent dropbacks and the pass-rush versus protection matchup, field goals follow stalled drives inside the kicker's range, two-point tries follow score and coaching tendency. Weather delays follow the forecast and venue. Counts are over-dispersed and depend on tempo and expected game script.

inputs.why: Plays per game bound every count.
Drives per game set opportunities for field goals and turnovers.
Pressure and sack rates drive sacks and interceptions.
Turnover rates regress, so counts should not extrapolate recent luck.
Havoc rate is the stable part of takeaway ability.
Kicker range and accuracy price field-goal counts.
Red-zone conversion decides field goal versus touchdown.
Script sets pass volume and two-point decisions (rebuilt from own forecast).
Forecast vintages drive weather-delay markets.
Crew tendencies change penalties and tempo.
Overtime adds possessions and two-point attempts.
Clock rules regime changes plays per game.
Sets the number of opportunities for the defensive count series (sacks, interceptions, forced turnovers).
Separates the quarterback component from the opposing rush in the team sack total.
Gives a regressed intensity for the interception and turnover series instead of extrapolating noisy interception counts.
Directly produces the mean and dispersion for TEAMFG and TOTALFG.
Provides P(at least one successful conversion in regulation), the strike of KXNCAAF2PT, from a small-count model.
Replaces a wind-focused weather input with the hazard that actually determines the delay series.
Gives the mean and spread of KXNCAAFTEAMYDS, which defines team yards as rushing plus receiving yards with sacks and kneels as negative rushing yards.

interactions.hypothesis: Pressure converts to sacks and takeaways most for high-havoc defences.
Trailing teams run more plays and attempt more fourth downs, raising counts together.
Wind compresses kicking range and shifts field-goal attempts to other decisions.

Expected sacks equal dropbacks times pressure rate times sack-given-pressure, and a mobile quick-release quarterback cuts the third factor, so the pass rush's advantage is large only against a quarterback who holds the ball; the effect is multiplicative in the volume.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit sacks per game on dropbacks x pressure x QB sack-given-pressure terms; compare additive and multiplicative forms by held-out deviance.

interactions.hypothesis: A field goal beyond about 40 yards is sharply less likely in a headwind of 15 mph or more, so wind turns long attempts into punts or fourth-down tries and both lowers makes and shifts attempts, which a make-rate adjustment alone misses.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare attempts and makes by distance bucket in windy versus calm games, split by kicker long-range accuracy.

interactions.hypothesis: Two-point attempts occur after touchdowns and are concentrated in specific score-differential states (down 8, up 17, trailing late), so the count depends on touchdowns and on the state at the time; a team that scores often when trailing is likely to try more.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate attempt probability by score-differential state and period and compare with the predicted count for teams with different scoring and trailing profiles.

interactions.hypothesis: A quarterback's observed interceptions carry little additional information beyond about 150 attempts once turnover-worthy play rate is known, and defensive havoc adds little to the interception rate beyond regression; forced-turnover counts are dominated by regression to the mean after the first handful of observations.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the regression coefficient of past INT rate by attempts played; test the incremental contribution of havoc to next-game interceptions.

interactions.hypothesis: Delays cluster in afternoon and evening games in warm months at open stadiums; the hazard is near zero in domes and cold weather, and the regime depends on the season month and stadium type, so a single weather forecast variable is not enough.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute delay frequency by month, local time and roof status over past seasons; confirm the regime separation.

nonlinearities.shape: Rare-event logistic in forecast thunderstorm probability with an afternoon peak and a floor at zero for domes
nonlinearities.why: Delay probability stays under a few percent until thunderstorm probability is high, then rises quickly; domes break the relationship, so the response is not linear in forecast probability.

nonlinearities.shape: Make probability decreasing in distance with steeper fall beyond 45 yards and an interaction with wind
nonlinearities.why: A kicker's accuracy is high inside 35 yards and drops steeply beyond 45, so the count of made field goals depends on the distribution of distances, not only the number of attempts.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise in lead size: dropbacks rise when trailing by two scores and fall when leading
nonlinearities.why: Opportunity counts for sacks and interceptions respond non-linearly to the expected margin, so the same team gets very different counts in a blowout and a close game.

mechanism_review.summary: Each series is a count of a discrete event over a team's or the game's opportunities: sacks and interceptions are rates times the opponent's dropbacks, with the rate set by the pass rush against the quarterback's sack and interception propensity; forced turnovers add fumble recoveries, which are roughly even odds and regress; field goals are attempts (drives that stall inside range and the coach's decision to kick) times make probability by distance and conditions; two-point conversions are touchdowns times a decision rate times success; interceptions gained are opponent dropbacks times the quarterback's interception rate. Weather delay is a different kind of event: a thunderstorm and lightning hazard at the venue during the game window. Counts are small and overdispersed, and each series' rules fix the overtime scope and exclusions.

stages.name: Opportunity counts for the event
stages.description: Each count has its own opportunity base: the opponent's dropbacks for sacks and interceptions, the team's drives that reach field-goal range for kicks, and the touchdowns scored for two-point tries. The base depends on tempo, run-pass mix and expected score state, and varies by 10 to 20 percent between games, giving the first source of variance.
stages.distribution: Counts with negative-binomial variation around a state-dependent mean; opportunity counts differ across series.

stages.name: Event rate per opportunity
stages.description: The rate per opportunity depends on matchup: the opposing pass rush against the protection and the quarterback's sack proneness, the quarterback's interception propensity against ball skills, the kicker's range and conditions for field goals, and the offence and defence for two-point success. Fumble recoveries are close to a coin flip and so forced-turnover rate regresses strongly.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli per opportunity with small probabilities (a few percent for sacks and interceptions); heavily regressed for lucky components.

stages.name: Decisions that create or remove opportunities
stages.description: Field-goal counts depend on the coach's choice to kick, go for it or punt on fourth down; two-point counts depend on the score chart and coach tendency; sack and interception counts depend on how often the opponent chooses to drop back. These choices are not random draws from an ability rate but strategy, and they change count distributions even at equal ability.
stages.distribution: Discrete decisions with coach-specific policy; conditional on score, time and field position.

stages.name: Environment and rare weather events
stages.description: Wind, temperature and rain change field-goal accuracy, passing and sacks; thunderstorms and lightning within the venue protocol radius cause delays, a binary event driven by convective weather, time of day and stadium type, where the series counts any official stoppage or delayed start for weather with no minimum duration.
stages.distribution: Continuous weather effects on rates; rare binary delay event with seasonal and diurnal pattern.

stages.name: Count distribution and settlement ambiguity
stages.description: The distribution of a small count is overdispersed and lumpy, and the rules set series-specific definitions that must be applied exactly: turnovers gained without turnovers on downs, nothing counted on 2-point tries, overtime scope that differs by series (periods one and two for sacks, interceptions and turnovers; any overtime for field goals; none for the two-point series) and any weather delay for the delay series.
stages.distribution: Negative binomial or Poisson-gamma counts with series-specific definitions; definition errors shift rung probabilities by amounts comparable to model edges.

talent_strength.note: Defensive havoc and kicker quality as unit strength for the counts.

opponent_matchup.note: Pass rush versus protection and quarterback traits.

role_personnel.note: Quarterback and kicker identity for each series.

availability_news.note: Partly covered: the pregame personnel vintage dataset (quarterback, kicker and pass-rusher status) feeds cfb.qb_status_pit, the quarterback sack and interception inputs and cfb.kicker; the size of the shift relative to small-count noise is untested (availability_effect), and pass-rusher status has no dedicated input.

environment.note: Wind effects on kicking and thunderstorm hazard for delays.

game_context_script.note: Score state drives pass volume and two-point decisions.

efficiency_conversion.note: Rates per opportunity with regression of lucky components.

distribution_variance.note: Overdispersed small counts with series-specific overtime scope.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest, rivalry and bowl stakes change effort and lineup but there is no argument that they change event counts like sacks, field goals or delays separately from the game-level scoring and tempo expectation, which the opportunity inputs already carry.

officiating_rules.note: Penalty tendency, overtime and clock rules; the delay protocol is a rule of the weather hazard input.

settlement_contract.note: Series definitions read from rules: turnovers gained excluding turnovers on downs, nothing counted on 2-point tries, overtime scope by series, regulation-only two-point conversions, any weather delay.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Seven team or game count series, each read from its own rules: TEAMINT, TEAMSACK and TEAMTO (defensive interceptions, sacks and turnovers gained by the named team; overtime periods one and two count; statistics during 2-point attempts excluded; a turnover on downs is not a turnover), TEAMFG and TOTALFG (made field goals by one team or both, overtime counts), KXNCAAF2PT (at least one successful 2-point conversion in regulation; overtime conversions do not count), and KXNCAAFDELAY (any official weather delay, including a delayed start or a stoppage after kickoff; non-weather delays resolve No). Postponement under 48 hours stays open, longer resolves to a fair price. KXNCAAFTEAMYDS moved to game_stat_props.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official game statistics (the number recorded by the team in the game) and, for DELAY, an official delay; the sampled text names no stats provider and no source for the delay declaration.
variants_and_edge_cases: Overtime scope differs by series: sacks, interceptions and turnovers count only overtime periods one and two, field-goal series count overtime without that limit (only periods one and two can produce field goals anyway), and the two-point series is regulation only.

KXNCAAFTEAMINT counts the named team's defensive interceptions; an interception on a 2-point try does not count, and since interceptions are also turnovers gained, TEAMINT and TEAMTO for the same team are nested counts.

TEAMTO counts turnovers gained (interceptions and fumble recoveries) and excludes turnovers on downs and possession changes after scores; the sampled secondary text is truncated, so fumbles lost on punts and kickoffs may be included or not and this is unconfirmed.

DELAY resolves YES for any official weather delay, including a delayed start, with no minimum duration and no source named in the sample for what counts as official; delays caused solely by other reasons resolve No.
Team-level counts (TEAMSACK, TEAMINT, TEAMTO, TEAMFG) are for the named team while TOTALFG and 2PT are for both teams; each series ladders thresholds as half-point strikes (3.5, 1.5, 2.5).

coaching_and_governance_events.label: College football coaching, transfer and conference-governance events
coaching_and_governance_events.target: Whether a named personnel, transfer or governance event happens by a stated date, or which person fills a role.
coaching_and_governance_events.mechanism: These events are not determined by game results alone: coach exits follow record against expectation, buyout cost and ownership signals; transfers follow roster need, name-image-likeness resources and portal windows; conference and playoff decisions follow governance calendars and voting rules. The prior is a reference-class base rate updated by dated reporting, not a game model.

inputs.why: Historical frequency of the event class by calendar window is the prior.
Coach tenure, record versus expectation and scheme changes drive exits.
Season outcome relative to expectation triggers decisions.
Stakes and rivalry outcomes shape pressure.
Roster churn and portal windows drive transfer markets.
Departure patterns inform roster-move markets.
Eligibility events change who can move or play.
Returning production signals retention pressure.
Format rules and approval processes drive playoff-structure markets.
Supplies the hazard process behind two series where the window end date is the main difference.
Separates ability to pay from desire to fire; a key friction missing from base rates.
Outcome is a categorical hire among named people with leakage through reporting; needs a candidate-level model.
Creates a structured state variable out of otherwise qualitative news for governance contracts.
The existing team-level transfer input is too aggregate for a named-player market.
Converts qualitative realignment talk into feasibility and timing constraints.
KXNCAAFDRAFTDECLARE settles on an unequivocal public declaration for the 2027 regular NFL Draft after issuance and before Feb 2, 2027, and the TRANSFER declare leg uses the same propensity.

interactions.hypothesis: Exit probability rises when record falls short of preseason expectation, especially late in the season.
Portal-window timing concentrates transfer announcements.
Rivalry losses raise exit risk beyond record alone.

A poor season raises the firing hazard but a large buyout multiplies it down, so the hazard is the product of performance shortfall and affordability; a coach with a 10 win shortfall and a 40 million dollar buyout is about as likely to survive as one with a smaller shortfall and no buyout.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit the hazard with an interaction of shortfall and buyout ratio; test in a historical sample of coaches with deep shortfalls.

interactions.hypothesis: The hazard changes regime at the end of the regular season: before rivalry week exits are rare, after the final regular-season game and after bowls they cluster, so the cumulative probability to Dec 1 is dominated by the last two weeks while to Feb 1 it includes the post-bowl wave.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate weekly hazard from the historical timing of FBS firings and test whether a regime break occurs around rivalry week.

interactions.hypothesis: CFP approval jumps when declared support crosses the voting threshold and the calendar allows a meeting; until then the probability is low regardless of rhetoric, so the key variable is votes relative to the threshold, not general support.
interactions.how_to_test: Code stakeholder positions in past governance decisions and estimate approval probability against votes minus threshold.

interactions.hypothesis: A candidate's hire probability depends on his own school's buyout and whether his current team is still playing, since coaches in the playoff or bowl cannot be hired until the season ends; the timing hazard and the candidate identity are interdependent.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare hire timing and identity for candidates at schools still playing versus eliminated, from past carousels.

interactions.hypothesis: A conference move has zero probability before the grant-of-rights, notice and membership-vote constraints allow it and a small positive hazard afterwards, so the response to reported talks is piecewise in the date and in the constraint state; the same rumor means very different things before and after the feasibility date.
interactions.how_to_test: Tabulate historical realignments by whether constraints had lapsed at announcement; estimate hazards before and after the feasibility date.

interactions.hypothesis: For a player listed in both KXNCAAFTRANSFER and a draft-declaration market, the declare leg of the transfer market and the DRAFTDECLARE YES are one event, so the transfer destination probabilities must be conditional on not declaring and the two markets must sum consistently.
interactions.how_to_test: For players with both markets, check that P(declare) in the declaration model equals the declare-leg probability and that destination probabilities renormalise over the non-declare mass.

nonlinearities.shape: Hazard convex in season shortfall and strongly time-clustered at the end of the regular season
nonlinearities.why: Mild underperformance rarely leads to a firing but large shortfalls with a poor finish carry steeply higher hazard, concentrated in a handful of days, so linear time-in-window accumulation is wrong.

nonlinearities.shape: Step at the approval threshold with a long flat region below it
nonlinearities.why: Governance outcomes do not move continuously with support: at 60 percent of required votes the probability is near zero and at 100 percent near one once a meeting occurs.

nonlinearities.shape: Winner-take-all softmax over candidates with rapid sharpening as credible reports accumulate
nonlinearities.why: Candidate probabilities start diffuse and collapse toward one name after a credible report, a non-linear update that a linear aggregation of rumors would miss.

mechanism_review.summary: These contracts depend on decisions by people and institutions made under constraints that can be written down: a head coach leaves when performance relative to expectation, contract cost, administration and outside opportunities combine to cross a decision threshold, concentrated at the end of the regular season and after bowls; a hire follows a vacancy through a candidate pool and a timing process; governance outcomes follow vote requirements and stakeholder positions on a meeting calendar; realignment follows contracts and procedures; a player's destination follows portal rules, need and compensation. Information arrives as dated reports, so the timing of information and the definition of which announcement counts are decisive.

stages.name: Triggering conditions relative to expectation
stages.description: Coach exits and some governance events are triggered when outcomes fall short of expectations: record against a preseason expectation, losing to a rival, missing a bowl. The trigger raises a decision-maker's willingness, but the realised decision is tempered by cost and calendar; expectation must be defined from ratings rather than from the final record alone.
stages.distribution: Hazard that increases with shortfall; concentrated in the last three weeks of the regular season and the first weeks after bowls.

stages.name: Constraints: cost, process and contracts
stages.description: A decision becomes feasible only if its cost is bearable: buyouts constrain firing, grant-of-rights and exit fees constrain conference moves, voting thresholds constrain CFP changes, and portal windows constrain transfers. These constraints are knowable from documents and calendars, and they change the date at which the event can first happen.
stages.distribution: Step functions in date: probability mass appears only after the feasibility date; before it the hazard is near zero.

stages.name: Candidate pool and destination choice
stages.description: When a vacancy opens or a player enters the portal, the outcome is categorical among a limited candidate set, determined by need, relationships, compensation and the competition among candidates; timing matters because a market can resolve No if no hire occurs before the date. For a draft declaration the choice is between returning, transferring and declaring, driven by draft projection, eligibility and college compensation, and the announcement window ends with the early-entry deadline in mid-January.
stages.distribution: Multinomial choice with a No-outcome mass for timing failure; sharp updating on credible reports.

stages.name: Information flow and credibility of reports
stages.description: Because decisions are private until announced, outcomes are forecast from reports of varying reliability; the timing of leaks (an AD meeting, a plane tracked, a source quoted) determines when probabilities should change. The rules define which announcements count, so a statement that does not meet the definition leaves the market open.
stages.distribution: Jump process in beliefs triggered by reports; reliability of sources varies by reporter; the event itself is a point-in-time announcement.

stages.name: Settlement definition and window
stages.description: Each rule picks a specific definition: announcement of future departure counts for coaches, binding adoption of exactly 24 teams for the CFP, announcement or formal notice for conferences, and the staying outcome for a transfer; windows end on specific dates (Dec 1, Dec 2, Jan 1, Feb 1, Feb 2, Sep 1), so the same underlying decision can resolve YES or NO depending on its timing.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping from the event time and type to the contract outcome.

talent_strength.note: Team strength matters only through performance relative to preseason expectation for coach exits; no player or team strength input applies to governance or realignment series.

opponent_matchup.note: There is no opponent or unit interaction in a personnel, governance or realignment decision; matchup structure is irrelevant to when a coach is fired or a conference votes.

role_personnel.note: Candidate and destination pools by role and need.

availability_news.note: Dated reports and statements fix the information set; source reliability weights are part of the candidate and governance models.

coaching_scheme.note: Coach tenure and results; scheme and tempo content of cfb.coaching is irrelevant here.

environment.note: Venue, weather and altitude play no role in whether a coach leaves, a conference realigns or the CFP changes its format; the only environment is institutional (market and media-rights context), which is handled by the governance state.

game_context_script.note: In-game flow does not apply; the only game-linked effect is that a single result (a rivalry loss or a lost bowl-eligibility game) can trigger a decision, which is carried by the expectation-shortfall and rivalry features.

pace_volume.note: There is no count of opportunities or possessions; these are binary or categorical decisions with a time window, so pace and volume do not describe the outcome process.

efficiency_conversion.note: No per-play rate exists; the closest analogue is the hit rate of reporters' leaks, which sits in the information-flow stage rather than in a performance conversion input.

distribution_variance.note: Calendar-aware base rates and hazards with uncertainty from small samples (15-25 FBS coach changes per year).

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Stakes, contract incentives and expectation shortfall.

officiating_rules.note: Governance rules: voting thresholds, grant-of-rights and CFP format procedure sit in the vote-count and feasibility states; cfb.playoff_format is only a format table (KEEP_CONTEXT) and is not credited as the governance layer, since expansion is a governing-body vote.

settlement_contract.note: Qualifying announcement definitions and window end dates read from the sampled rules text.

contract_review.settlement_definition: These are event-by-date or categorical outcomes decided by people and institutions, not by a game: KXNCAAFCOACHLEAVE and COACHOUT settle YES if the named head coach is fired, resigns, otherwise leaves, or announces he will leave before the stated date (Dec 1, 2026 or Feb 1, 2027); KXNCAAFNEXTCOACH settles YES if the next permanent head coach officially announced is the named person (interim or acting coaches do not count) and resolves No if none is announced before Sep 1, 2027; KXNCAAFCFPEXPAND settles YES if the CFP has officially approved a fully adopted format with exactly 24 teams, confirmed by a Source Agency, after issuance and before Dec 2, 2026; CONFLEAVE and JOINCONF settle on an announcement, binding agreement, formal notice or settlement within the period even if the effective date is later; KXNCAAFTRANSFER is a multi-outcome market on a named player's destination. KXNCAAFDRAFTDECLARE (moved here by the reconciliation) settles YES if the named player publicly and unequivocally announces entry into the 2027 regular NFL Draft after issuance and before Feb 2, 2027; rumours or 'considering' statements do not count and a later reversal does not undo a declaration.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Source Agencies named in the rules (credible news reports, official school or conference announcements); the exact list of Source Agencies is not in the sampled text.
variants_and_edge_cases: Coach-exit contracts differ only by named coach and window end (Dec 1 vs Feb 1), so the hazard must be integrated to the exact date; announcement of future departure counts, so a mid-season announced retirement resolves immediately.
NEXTCOACH resolves No for all candidates if no permanent coach is announced before Sep 1, 2027, and an interim hire does not count; candidates are mutually exclusive except through that No state.
CFPEXPAND needs a binding decision by an authorized governing body with exactly 24 teams confirmed by a Source Agency before Dec 2, 2026; the decision may take effect in a later season.

CONFLEAVE and JOINCONF are triggered by announcement, binding agreement, formal notice or settlement, not by effective membership change. Four sampled secondary texts are cut at 600 characters: CONFLEAVE (further triggers may exist), TRANSFER (the commits-elsewhere clause is cut mid-sentence), CFPEXPAND (the clause defining how distinct teams are counted, including an opening round, is cut) and DRAFTDECLARE (cut after the supplemental-draft note); COACHLEAVE, COACHOUT, NEXTCOACH and JOINCONF texts are complete.

TRANSFER outcomes are multi-way (stays, declares for the draft, commits elsewhere, possibly other); sum of probabilities must be one when all outcomes are listed, and the staying outcome is conditional on the portal behaviour.

DRAFTDECLARE and the declare leg of TRANSFER are the same kind of event (an unequivocal public declaration); both now sit in this archetype and must use one declaration model, while only the regular NFL Draft counts (the supplemental draft does not).

half_full_double_result.label: CFB half-time/full-time double result
half_full_double_result.target: Probability of a stated (1st-half result, full-game result) pair, half ties allowed, full game incl. OT.
half_full_double_result.mechanism: Each market is one cell of a six-cell partition (3 half states x 2 full-game winners): first-half result (team A leads, tie, team B leads) crossed with the full-game winner, which always exists because overtime is included. The cell probability is P(half state) times P(full winner | half state). The first factor comes from a lumpy half-margin distribution built from the strength gap, team half-scoring splits and possession order; the second comes from second-half and overtime play given the half state, where leaders slow down, trailing teams take risk, starters are pulled in blowouts, and the team that did not receive the opening kickoff usually receives the second-half kickoff (toss winners normally defer, so this is a convention, not a rule). Reversal cells (half leader loses) and tie-at-half cells carry the mass a product of marginals misprices.

inputs.why: Non-market composite rating sets the full-game expected margin from which both half and full-game outcome probabilities are built.
Opponent-adjusted offensive efficiency shows how quickly each side scores early, which shapes the half-margin spread around the strength gap.
Opponent-adjusted defensive efficiency completes the per-drive scoring rates used for both halves of the joint simulation.
Confirmed starting QB at decision time moves both the half and full-game margin; a backup changes the reversal likelihood too.
Team-specific first versus second half scoring shares (fast starters, late surgers) move the half margin away from half the full margin.
Discrete half-margin mass at 0 and key numbers gives the half-tie leg (Tie 1H) its probability, which a normal approximation misstates.
For the tie-at-half cells, P(team wins | tied half) is the second factor of the joint and is not the unconditional win probability.
Six-cell conditional of full-game winner given half bucket and rating gap (the zero bucket is delegated to the tie-conditional input); the core joint-dependence input of this contract.
The opening-kick choice (toss winners usually defer) decides who gets the extra first-half drive and the second-half kickoff, linking half and second-half margins.
End-of-half drives decide many half leads and ties because they occur after the clock budget is already partly used.
Starter removal with big second-half leads caps reversals in mismatches and truncates margin growth after halftime.
Trailing teams speed up and leaders slow down after halftime, which changes the number of second-half drives available for a comeback.
Aggressive fourth-down policy raises second-half variance for the trailing side, fattening the reversal cells.
Full-game result includes overtime, so tied regulation games must be resolved by the college OT format into a winner.
Converts a regulation tie into a full-game winner probability through alternating-possession OT scoring.
Home field shifts both halves; neutral sites (bowls, CFP) remove it and change the tie-at-half winner tilt.
Wind and rain lower scoring, which raises half-tie mass and compresses margins in both halves.
Tests whether staff identity tilts reversals after halftime beyond the rating gap; heavily shrunk.
The rules define the cell pair (half result incl. tie, full game incl. OT) and the 48-hour postponement clause.
Settled result per cell is needed to verify that the six-cell partition (3 half states x 2 winners) sums to one on Kalshi settlement.
Plays per game and tempo set how many drives each half contains, which bounds half-margin spread and tie mass.
Combined drives per half decide how many scoring events can occur before the break and hence tie mass at zero.
Probability that four quarters end level converts into overtime weight on the full-game winner leg, conditional on half state.
Two-point success from the third overtime decides long overtimes, a rare tail of the full-game winner leg.
Starters and role changes beyond the QB (OL, defensive front) shift strength in both halves.
Coach tempo, fourth-down and blowout behaviour regimes shape second-half script and reversal tails.
Points per scoring opportunity decides how half drives convert into points, so TD-versus-FG lumpiness of the half margin.
Clock-rule regime (2023 first-down clock change) alters drives per half, so pooled history needs regime indicators.
Postponement and cancellation events decide whether the 48-hour clause or the truncated fallback applies to open cells.
Option or tempo offences against unfamiliar defences change early-half scoring and adjustment room.
Chance the starting QB or key players leave mid-game moves the second-half regime and reversal tail.
Postseason opt-outs change strength for bowl and CFP games where this series also lists cells.
Rivalry, stakes and postseason layoffs affect early scoring and late effort.
Bye, short week and travel shift both halves modestly and postseason layoffs shift first-half sharpness.

A targeting disqualification in the second half of the previous game suspends the player for the first half only, so it shifts the half leg but not the second half; the half and full-game legs move by different amounts.

interactions.hypothesis: A half lead protects less when the leader is the weaker team: reversal probability rises with the pre-game gap against the half leader.
Wind or rain lowers half scoring and raises the zero-margin mass, enlarging every Tie 1H cell non-linearly.
Starter removal after a large half lead truncates second-half margin and pushes reversal cells toward zero beyond what rate models imply.

The team that usually receives the second-half kickoff (the one that did not take the opening kick) gets the first second-half possession after a tied half, tilting the two tie-at-half cells toward it beyond the rating gap.

The probability that the half leader holds on depends on who leads: a 7-point half lead by a 17-point favourite converts at very high rates, the same lead by an underdog converts far less often because the stronger team gets more second-half scoring drives. The reversal cell is a function of half margin and gap jointly, not additive.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit win|half margin with and without a half-margin x rating-gap term on 2014+ FBS games; compare log loss on held-out seasons.

interactions.hypothesis: Sustained wind above about 15 mph and heavy rain lower first-half scoring; the probability of a tied half rises faster than linearly as expected half total falls toward 14 because 0-0, 3-3 and 7-7 halves become common.
interactions.how_to_test: Bin games by kickoff wind and precipitation; compare observed half-tie frequency against a lattice fitted without weather, by expected-total bin.

interactions.hypothesis: Once the half lead exceeds about three scores, backups enter during the third quarter and the leader stops scoring, but the trailing team also faces a large deficit; reversal cells collapse to near zero above that threshold while margin cells become unreliable.
interactions.how_to_test: Plot P(reversal) by half margin with a change-point fit; check whether the drop location differs for coaches with early versus late starter pull.

interactions.hypothesis: After a tied half, the team receiving the second-half kickoff gets the first and often an extra possession; its conditional win probability is higher than the opponent's at equal strength, so the two tie-at-half cells split unevenly by who deferred.
interactions.how_to_test: Among halves tied at the break, regress full-game win on second-half receiver indicator plus rating gap and home flag.

interactions.hypothesis: A trailing team that both speeds up and goes for it on fourth down raises second-half variance on two axes; the comeback probability scales with the product of extra drives and per-drive upside, so an aggressive up-tempo underdog fattens reversal cells far more than either trait alone.
interactions.how_to_test: Interact trailing-team second-half seconds per play with fourth-down go rate in the reversal model; compare to main-effects-only fit.

nonlinearities.shape: logistic in half margin, steepest between -7 and +7
nonlinearities.why: Each additional point of half lead is worth most when the half is within one score; beyond 15 points win probability saturates near one, so reversal cells are concentrated in one-score halves.

nonlinearities.shape: spike at zero decaying with absolute expected margin
nonlinearities.why: Half-tie probability falls sharply as the expected half margin moves away from zero and also as expected half total rises, so Tie 1H cells are much more valuable in close low-scoring games than a linear rule suggests.

nonlinearities.shape: step: regulation tie maps to one winner
nonlinearities.why: The overtime inclusion turns a regulation tie into a full-game win for one side, adding a discrete chunk of probability to the two winner cells that is absent if OT were excluded.

mechanism_review.summary: The outcome is a pair drawn from the joint law of (first-half margin, final margin after overtime). Start from team strength to get expected margin and total. Split expected scoring into halves using team-specific half shares and possession order; the half margin is a discrete, lumpy variable with real mass at zero in close, low-total games. The second half is then played conditional on the half state: leaders shorten the game, trailing teams pass and go for it on fourth down, starters come out in blowouts, and the team that did not take the opening kickoff (usually after a deferral) gets the second-half kickoff. Regulation ties go to college overtime with alternating possessions and two-point shootouts from the third OT. The joint therefore has positive dependence (half leaders usually win) with reversal tails that depend on the strength gap and script, which independence of halves misprices.

stages.name: Full-game strength gap and scoring environment
stages.description: Non-market team ratings, opponent-adjusted offensive and defensive efficiency, confirmed quarterbacks and venue set the expected final margin and total. These two numbers determine how often a half is close enough to tie and how large half leads tend to be, and are the conditioning variables for reversal rates in the second half.
stages.distribution: Expected margin is continuous but final margins are fat-tailed with key-number clustering at 3, 7, 10 and 14.

stages.name: First-half margin with tie mass
stages.description: First-half margin comes from roughly five to seven drives per team: team half-scoring shares (fast starters versus slow starters), who gets the opening kickoff and the extra drive, scripted openers and the end-of-half two-minute drive. The result is a lattice of 3- and 7-point steps with a material probability of exactly zero, highest when the expected margin is small and the total low or weather suppresses scoring. A targeting carry-over suspension removes a player for this half only, so the half margin can shift without a matching shift in the second half.
stages.distribution: Discrete lattice with spikes at 0, +/-3, +/-7; tie mass in close games is a hypothesis (order of ten percent) not yet measured; to be checked on CFBD line scores, 2023+ clock-rule seasons, smaller in mismatches.

stages.name: Second half conditional on the half state
stages.description: Given the half margin, the second half changes regime: leaders run the ball and slow the clock, trailing teams pass and go for it on fourth down, large leads trigger starter removal, and the team that did not take the opening kickoff (usually via a toss-winner deferral) receives the second-half kickoff. These behaviours set the reversal probability (half leader loses) and the winner split after a tied half, which together are the off-diagonal cells of the six-cell table.
stages.distribution: Conditional win probability is sigmoid in half margin, shifted by pregame gap; reversal tails thin out quickly beyond two scores.

stages.name: Overtime resolution of regulation ties
stages.description: Because the full game includes overtime, regulation ties are converted into a winner through the college format: alternating possessions from the 25, mandatory two-point tries from the second OT and two-point shootouts from the third. Kicking and red-zone offence tilt the winner away from 50/50, and the probability of reaching OT depends on the regulation tie curve, which is linked to the half state.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli winner with mild skill tilt; reached in a few percent of games, more in close low-total matchups.

stages.name: Settlement of the cell
stages.description: The market pays only if both legs match. The partition identity (all six cells sum to one) is a hard coherence constraint, a postponement within 48 hours keeps the market alive, and beyond 48 hours the sampled fallback wording is cut off. Settlement depends on the official half-time and final score, with overtime counted for the full-game leg only.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping from (half margin sign, final winner) to YES/NO; rare void path on cancellation.

coaching_scheme.note: Tempo, aggression and after-half adjustments shape reversal cells.

environment.note: Home field and weather shift both halves and half-tie mass.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Each KXNCAAF1HFT market names a pair: a 1st-half result (one team leads, or the 1st half is tied) and a full-game winner, with the full game including overtime. YES only if both legs are correct; any other combination is NO. Because overtime is included the full-game leg has no tie, so the series partitions into six cells per game (3 half states: team A leads, tie, team B leads; x 2 full-game winners). If the game is postponed but starts within 48 hours it settles on the official final; beyond 48 hours the sampled text is truncated ('resolve to a fai...'), so the exact fallback (likely a fair-price settlement) cannot be read. The settlement data source is not visible in the sample.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official final and half-time score of the game; the sampled rules do not name the source agency (truncated), so the resolving provider is unverified.
variants_and_edge_cases: Tie-at-half cells: the half leg can be a tie (e.g. 'Tie 1H / Notre Dame game'), so the half margin's mass at exactly zero matters, including 0-0 halves.
Overtime: full game includes OT, so a regulation tie is not a NO for both winner cells; one of the two tie-in-regulation paths resolves via the college OT format.
Postponement: game starting within 48 hours of original time stays open and settles on the official final; the beyond-48-hours outcome text is truncated in the sample.
Only one series with one sampled market (the TIEND cell); it is unknown whether every game lists all six half/full cells or only a subset (matters for coherence checks across cells).

multi_leg_parlay_packs.label: College football pre-packaged parlays (multi-game moneyline and same-game combos)
contract_types: MVE NCAAF Pre Pack (same-game spread + total)
multi_leg_parlay_packs.target: Probability that every leg of a pre-packaged combination resolves YES jointly: several named teams all win their games, or a spread cover and a total side in the same game both hit.
multi_leg_parlay_packs.mechanism: A pack pays only if every leg hits, so its probability is the joint of leg events, not a single game outcome. For multi-game moneyline packs each leg is a game winner (always decided via overtime); legs are independent in game noise but share rating-model error through conference offsets in cross-conference postseason games; the dependence is signed by the conference exposure of each backed side (a Big Ten offset error helps a leg backing Indiana over Alabama and hurts a leg backing Texas Tech over Oregon), and opt-out waves add slate-wide shocks. Inputs apply by contract type: cross-game inputs (cross_game_residual_dependence, rating_posterior_draws, cross_conf_calibration, rest_travel) to the 2/3/4-leg moneyline packs; margin_total_joint_pmf, expected_possessions, weather_pit, blowout_management to the same-game pack. For same-game packs the legs (spread cover and total side) are strongly dependent through pace and score state: underdog cover pairs with the under, favourite cover with the over. Errors in each leg compound multiplicatively, so calibration of every leg and of the dependence matters more than in a single-game market.

inputs.why: Non-market strength for each leg's team pair is the base of every leg probability in the pack.
Opponent-adjusted offence sets both the margin and the total of a same-game leg pair.
Opponent-adjusted defence completes the per-leg expected margin and total.
[ML packs] Postseason legs pit conferences that rarely meet; mis-set offsets bias legs in signed directions by conference.
[ML packs] Upstream joint rating draws from which the leg-pair matrix is computed; not counted separately from that matrix.
[ML packs] Signed leg-pair correlation matrix from conference exposure of each backed side, replacing the independence assumption.
[SGP] Joint margin-total probability at the spread and total strikes of the same-game pack; owns the score-covariance mechanism.
A starting QB change in any leg moves that leg and so the whole conjunction; postseason QB opt-outs and transfers are common.

[ML packs, SGP] Interim coaches after postseason coaching changes and tempo choices affect leg strength and totals.
